Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 10, verses 1–2:

Explanation of the words:

Alif-Lam-Ra (الر): This is the fourth surah among the surahs that open with the disjointed letters. It is written الر and read Alif, Lam, Ra.

The Book (الكتاب): That is, the Great Qur'an.

The Wise (الحكيم): The one that speaks with wisdom. The Qur'an contains wise principles, so it is wise (hakim) and also firmly structured (muhkam).

Wonder (عجباً): The wonder (al-'ajab) is that at which one marvels.

A man from among them (رجل منهم): This is Muhammad ﷺ.

A sure standing (قدم صدق): That is, a good reward for what they sent forward in their lives of faith and righteous deeds.

Indeed, this (إن هذا): That is, the Qur'an.

Clear magic (لسحر مبين): That is, manifestly clear, with no concealment, in their lying and their baseless claims.

The meaning of the two verses:

Among the matters addressed by the Meccan surahs are the questions of monotheism, revelation, and the Final Resurrection. Surah Yunus opens with the matter of revelation, that is, its affirmation and establishment from God to His Messenger Muhammad ﷺ. God the Exalted says: ﴿Alif, Lam, Ra. These are the verses of the Wise Book﴾, meaning: these are the verses of the noble Qur'an, whose verses are firmly structured, containing many wise principles, to the extent that it is as if it were the Wise One who places everything in its proper place. And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Is it a wonder for the people that We have revealed to a man from among them﴾, meaning: Was Our revelation to Muhammad, Our servant and Messenger, who is a man from Quraysh, a wonder for the people of Mecca that they marvel at? The revealed content is: ﴿that warn the people﴾, that is, frighten them of the consequence of association with God, disbelief, and disobedience, ﴿and give good tidings to those who believe﴾, that is, that they will have a sure standing with their Lord, which is the good reward for the faith and righteous deeds they sent forward, which they will receive on the day they meet their Lord in the Hereafter. When he ﷺ warned and gave good tidings, the disbelievers said, "This is clear magic," and at another time they said, "He is a clear magician." Their saying this was merely to repel the truth and refuse to accept it, not because what he warned of and gave good tidings of is magic, nor because the one who warned and gave good tidings is a magician. Rather, it is obstinacy, denial, and arrogance from the people of association, disbelief, falsehood, evil, and corruption.

Lessons from the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1. Affirmation of the doctrine of revelation by the testimony of the Book that was revealed.

2. Establishing the prophethood of Muhammad ﷺ and affirming it through the revelation sent to him.

3. Clarifying the mission of the Messenger ﷺ, which is warning and giving good tidings.

4. Good tidings to the people of faith and righteous deeds of what has been prepared for them with their Lord.

5. The disbelievers' lack of restraint in lying and deception.

Explanation of the Words:

Inna Rabbakumu Allah: That is, your true deity, whom you must worship alone, is Allah.

Khalaqa as-samawati wal-ard: That is, He brought them into existence from non-existence, when they were nothing, and they became worlds.

Fi sittati ayyam: These are Sunday, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday.

Thumma istawa 'alal-'arsh: That is, He established Himself upon the Throne in a manner befitting Him, the Mighty and Majestic; it is not said "how?"

Ma min shafi'in illa min ba'di idhnihi: That is, no one will intercede on the Day of Resurrection except after He gives him permission.

Afala tadhakkarun: That is, will you persist in your denial and obstinacy, so that you do not take heed?

Thumma yu'iduhu: That is, after annihilation and decay, and that is the Day of Resurrection.

Sharabun min hamim: That is, water that has been heated and boiled until it becomes scalding, scorching the faces.

Ja'alash-shamsa diya': That is, He made it give light upon the earth.

Wal-qamara nuran: That is, He made the moon with the light of the earth; and He is the One who created the light of the sun and the light of the moon.

Wa qaddarahu manazil: That is, He ordained the moon in stations, and the sun likewise.

Li ta'lamu: That is, He ordained them in stations so that people may know the number of years and the reckoning.

Yattaqun: That is, the displeasure and punishment of Allah, by obeying Him and obeying His Messenger.

Meaning of the Verses:

These verses establish divinity after the establishment and affirmation of revelation in the two preceding verses. The Exalted's saying, ﴿Indeed, your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days; then He established Himself above the Throne, arranging the affair﴾, is an announcement from Him, the Exalted, that He, the Mighty and Majestic, is the Lord, that is, the deity of those polytheists who take idols as gods alongside Him and worship them, though they have created nothing. As for Allah, He is the One who created the heavens and the earth in six days, by the measure of these days of ours, since there were not yet days like the days of this world at that time. Then He established Himself upon His Throne in a manner befitting His majesty and perfection, arranging the affair of the heavens and the earth. This is the true God who must be worshipped and drawn near to. And His saying: ﴿There is no intercessor except after His permission﴾ means that, in His greatness and the might of His dominion, no one can intercede for another except after He gives permission to him. So how then do they worship these idols, hoping for their intercession for their worshippers, when Allah is not approached for intercession by anyone except with His permission? And the Exalted's saying: ﴿That is Allah, your Lord, so worship Him﴾ means that this One described with these attributes and identified by these qualities of majesty and perfection is your true Lord, so worship Him by what He has prescribed for you of the various kinds of worship, that you may be perfected and made happy. And His saying: ﴿Will you not then take heed?﴾ is a rebuke to the polytheists: why do you not admonish yourselves after hearing the truth? And the Exalted's saying: ﴿To Him is your return, all of you; the promise of Allah is true﴾ establishes the principle of the final resurrection: Allah, the Exalted, your true Lord, is your Returner after your death, all of you, since He has promised you the true promise of returning to Him and standing before Him. And His saying: ﴿that He may reward those who believed and did righteous deeds with justice﴾ means with justice, and it explains the reason for life after death: this abode is a house of action, and the Hereafter is a house of recompense for that action. Therefore resurrection is obligatory and certain, and there is no way around it; and there is no sense in denying it, because the One Who is able to originate creation is able to restore it all the more. And the Exalted's saying: ﴿As for those who disbelieved, they will have a drink of scalding water and a painful punishment﴾ means: boiling water that has reached the extreme of heat, and a painful punishment, that is, a grievous one. It is an announcement from Him, the Exalted, of the recompense of the people of disbelief on the Day of Resurrection, and it is also a reason for life after death and resurrection after annihilation. Thus the principle of resurrection is established, just as the principle of monotheism was established before it, and the principle of revelation before that, since the Meccan surahs revolve around these matters. And the Exalted's saying: ﴿It is He who made the sun a radiance﴾ means possessing radiance, and the moon a light, possessing light, and He ordained for the moon stations, which are twenty-eight stations through which the moon moves. He did this ﴿so that you may know the number of years and the reckoning﴾, so that you may know the number of years, months, days and hours, since your lives need that. This Lord, who is capable of this creation and this management, is the true God who must be worshipped, and no one else should be worshipped. This is an establishment of monotheism and an affirmation of it.

And His saying: ﴿Allah did not create that except with truth﴾ means that He did not create this worldly life and these worlds in vain, to perish and decay after a while with nothing beyond it; rather He created that only with truth, that is, in order that He might command and forbid, then recompense the obedient for their obedience and the disobedient for their disobedience. This also affirms the matter of resurrection and recompense. And His saying: ﴿He details the signs﴾ means this detailing witnessed in this context. ﴿For a people who know﴾, since they are the ones who benefit from it; as for the ignorant, they do not benefit from this detailing and clarification. And the Exalted's saying in the last verse: ﴿Indeed, in the alternation of the night and the day﴾ means in their lengthening and shortening, their light and darkness, ﴿and what Allah has created in the heavens and the earth﴾ of orbs and stars, winds and rains, and what He has created on the earth of humans and animals, land and sea, rivers, trees, mountains and valleys, ﴿are signs﴾, that is, clear indications pointing to the Creator, the God who is truly worshipped, and to His majesty, beauty and perfection, and to the greatness of His power and the might of His dominion. Therefore He is worshipped with the utmost love, glorified with the utmost glorification, and feared with the utmost awe; He is remembered and not forgotten, thanked and not disbelieved, obeyed and not disobeyed. And the Exalted's saying: ﴿for a people who are mindful of Allah﴾ specifies the people of piety for these signs among the manifestations of His creation and power that were mentioned, because they are the ones who truly perceive and witness that, owing to the purity of their spirits and the cleanliness of their hearts and souls. As for the people of polytheism and sin, they are in a darkness in which they see nothing, and we seek refuge in Allah.

Guidance from the Verses:

1- The affirmation of Allah's divinity and that He is the true God.
2- The affirmation of the doctrine of resurrection and recompense in the Hereafter.
3- Explanation of the wisdom in the creation of the sun and moon and the ordaining of their stations.
4- The legitimacy of learning arithmetic and astronomy for what benefits the Muslims.
5- The virtue of knowledge and piety and of those among the believers who possess them.

So how then do they worship these idols, hoping for their intercession for their worshippers, when Allah is not approached for intercession by anyone except with His permission? And the Exalted's saying: ﴿That is Allah, your Lord, so worship Him﴾ means that this One described with these attributes and identified by these qualities of majesty and perfection is your true Lord, so worship Him by what He has prescribed for you of the various kinds of worship, that you may be perfected and made happy. And His saying: ﴿Will you not then take heed?﴾ is a rebuke to the polytheists: why do you not admonish yourselves after hearing the truth? And the Exalted's saying: ﴿To Him is your return, all of you; the promise of Allah is true﴾ establishes the principle of the final resurrection: Allah, the Exalted, your true Lord, is your Returner after your death, all of you, since He has promised you the true promise of returning to Him and standing before Him. And His saying: ﴿that He may reward those who believed and did righteous deeds with justice﴾ means with justice, and it explains the reason for life after death: this abode is a house of action, and the Hereafter is a house of recompense for that action. Therefore resurrection is obligatory and certain, and there is no way around it; and there is no sense in denying it, because the One Who is able to originate creation is able to restore it all the more. And the Exalted's saying: ﴿As for those who disbelieved, they will have a drink of scalding water and a painful punishment﴾ means: boiling water that has reached the extreme of heat, and a painful punishment, that is, a grievous one. It is an announcement from Him, the Exalted, of the recompense of the people of disbelief on the Day of Resurrection, and it is also a reason for life after death and resurrection after annihilation. Thus the principle of resurrection is established, just as the principle of monotheism was established before it, and the principle of revelation before that, since the Meccan surahs revolve around these matters. And the Exalted's saying: ﴿It is He who made the sun a radiance﴾ means possessing radiance, and the moon a light, possessing light, and He ordained for the moon stations, which are twenty-eight stations through which the moon moves. He did this ﴿so that you may know the number of years and the reckoning﴾, so that you may know the number of years, months, days and hours, since your lives need that. This Lord, who is capable of this creation and this management, is the true God who must be worshipped, and no one else should be worshipped. This is an establishment of monotheism and an affirmation of it.

And His saying: ﴿Allah did not create that except with truth﴾ means that He did not create this worldly life and these worlds in vain, to perish and decay after a while with nothing beyond it; rather He created that only with truth, that is, in order that He might command and forbid, then recompense the obedient for their obedience and the disobedient for their disobedience. This also affirms the matter of resurrection and recompense. And His saying: ﴿He details the signs﴾ means this detailing witnessed in this context. ﴿For a people who know﴾, since they are the ones who benefit from it; as for the ignorant, they do not benefit from this detailing and clarification. And the Exalted's saying in the last verse: ﴿Indeed, in the alternation of the night and the day﴾ means in their lengthening and shortening, their light and darkness, ﴿and what Allah has created in the heavens and the earth﴾ of orbs and stars, winds and rains, and what He has created on the earth of humans and animals, land and sea, rivers, trees, mountains and valleys, ﴿are signs﴾, that is, clear indications pointing to the Creator, the God who is truly worshipped, and to His majesty, beauty and perfection, and to the greatness of His power and the might of His dominion. Therefore He is worshipped with the utmost love, glorified with the utmost glorification, and feared with the utmost awe; He is remembered and not forgotten, thanked and not disbelieved, obeyed and not disobeyed. And the Exalted's saying: ﴿for a people who are mindful of Allah﴾ specifies the people of piety for these signs among the manifestations of His creation and power that were mentioned, because they are the ones who truly perceive and witness that, owing to the purity of their spirits and the cleanliness of their hearts and souls. As for the people of polytheism and sin, they are in a darkness in which they see nothing, and we seek refuge in Allah.

Guidance from the Verses:

1- The affirmation of Allah's divinity and that He is the true God.
2- The affirmation of the doctrine of resurrection and recompense in the Hereafter.
3- Explanation of the wisdom in the creation of the sun and moon and the ordaining of their stations.
4- The legitimacy of learning arithmetic and astronomy for what benefits the Muslims.
5- The virtue of knowledge and piety and of those among the believers who possess them.

**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 10, verses 7–10:**

**Explanation of the words:**

*La yarjuna liqa'ana* (﴿لا يرجون لقاءنا﴾): That is, they do not hope for or anticipate meeting Allah, the Exalted, on the Day of Resurrection.

*Wa radu bil-hayat al-dunya* (﴿ورضوا بالحياة الدنيا﴾): That is, they are content with this worldly life instead of the Hereafter, so they give no thought to the Abode of the Hereafter.

*Wa ṭma'annu biha* (﴿واطمأنوا بها﴾): That is, they settle down in it and incline to it, seeing no other life in which to labor.

*Ghafilun* (﴿غافلون﴾): They do not look at them (the signs) and do not reflect upon them.

*Ma'wahum al-nar* (﴿مأواهم النار﴾): That is, the Fire is the refuge to which they resort, and they have no other.

*Yahdihim rabbuhum bi-imanihim* (﴿يهديهم ربهم بإيمانهم﴾): That is, by making for them, because of their faith, a light by which they are guided to Paradise.

*Da'wahum fiha subhanaka Allahumma* (﴿دعواهم فيها سبحانك اللهم﴾): That is, they ask for whatever they wish with the phrase "Subhanaka Allahumma" (Glory be to You, O Allah).

*Wa akhiru da'wahum an al-hamdu lillah* (﴿وآخر دعواهم أن الحمد لله﴾): That is, the last of their supplication is: "All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds."

**Meaning of the verses:**

After establishing revelation and divinity in the preceding verses, the Exalted mentions in these three noble verses the recompense of each of two groups: those who denied the meeting with Allah, who did not hope for reward nor fear punishment, were content with the worldly life and settled in it; and those who believed in Allah, His meeting, His promise and His threat, believed in that, and did righteous deeds. The Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, those who do not expect to meet Us, and are content with the life of this world and feel at ease in it, and those who are heedless of Our signs﴾. That is, their souls have settled into it and they have truly inclined to it. ﴿And those who are heedless of Our signs﴾: that is, His signs in the cosmos across the horizons and in the Qur'an, which are the proofs of Allah, the Exalted, and His evidences indicating His existence, His oneness, His revelation and His law. They are heedless of them, not looking into them nor reflecting on what they indicate, because of their absorption in the world, where they have turned toward it and given it their hearts, their faces and all their limbs. Concerning these, the Exalted says regarding their recompense: ﴿Those—their refuge is the Fire, because of what they used to earn﴾: that is, of wrongdoing, evil and corruption. And the Exalted says regarding the recompense of those who believed in His meeting and hoped for what is with Him: ﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds—their Lord will guide them﴾: that is, to the path of Paradise ﴿by their faith﴾: that is, by the light of their faith, so they enter it. ﴿Rivers will flow beneath them in the Gardens of Bliss﴾. The bliss of Paradise is both spiritual and physical. The physical they obtain by their saying, "Subhanaka Allahumma"; when one of them says this phrase, every desire he has is present before him. The spiritual they obtain through the peace of Allah and His angels upon them: ﴿and their greeting therein is "Peace"﴾. And when they finish with food and drink, they say, "All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds." This is the meaning of His saying ﴿Their call therein is, "Glory be to You, O Allah"﴾: that is, their supplication, the form of their request. ﴿And their greeting therein is "Peace." And the last of their call﴾: that is, their supplication, ﴿is that﴾: that is, that: ﴿"All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds."﴾

**Guidance from the verses:**

1. Warning against forgetting the Hereafter, and against turning toward the world and chasing after its adornments.
2. Warning against heedlessness by not reflecting on the cosmic and Qur'anic signs, for this reflection is the path of guidance and salvation from error.
3. Faith and righteous deeds are the key to Paradise and the path leading to it.
4. The bliss of Paradise is spiritual and physical, and it is attained through three phrases:

"Subhanaka Allahumma," "Wa tahiyyatuhum fiha salam," and "Wa akhiru da'wahum an al-hamdu lillahi Rabbi al-'alamin."

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 10, verses 11–14:

Explanation of the words:

Al-sharr (evil): everything that causes harm to the intellect, the body, wealth or offspring; al-khayr (good) is its opposite: that which brings benefit to the body, wealth or offspring.

La-qudiya ilayhim ajalahum (Had He hastened for them their term): they would have been destroyed and died.

Fa-nadharu (So We leave): i.e., We abandon.

Fi tughyanihim ya'mahun (in their rebellion, wandering blindly): i.e., in their wrongdoing and disbelief they wander back and forth, unable to come out of it, like the blind.

Al-durr (affliction): sickness and everything that harms the body, wealth or offspring.

Marra ka'an lam yad'unā (he passes on as though he had never called upon Us): he continues in his disbelief and falsehood as though he had never been the one who called upon Us to remove his affliction.

Kadhalika zuyyina (Thus it was made attractive): like that forgetting, which is swift after he had called for its removal, the wrongdoing and evil were made attractive to the transgressors (al-musrifin) in their excess.

Al-qurun (the generations): i.e., the people of the generations.

Bil-bayyinat (with clear proofs): with the arguments and signs of the truth of their message.

Khala'if (successors): i.e., for you, whom you succeed after their destruction.

Meaning of the verses:

During the period in which this Meccan surah was being revealed, the polytheists of Mecca were in great agitation and turmoil, to the extent that they demanded that punishment be sent down upon them. God, exalted is He, mentioned this about them in more than one verse of His Book, among them: ﴿They ask for the punishment to hasten; and had there not been an appointed term, the punishment would have come upon them﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 53], and in this matter the words of God were revealed: ﴿And if God were to hasten for people the evil﴾, i.e., upon their asking Him for it, or their doing what calls for it, as He hastens good for them, ﴿He would surely have decreed for them their term﴾, i.e., they would have been destroyed with a general destruction and their term in this life would have ended. And His words: ﴿So We leave those who do not expect meeting Us in their rebellion, wandering blindly﴾, i.e., We did not hasten punishment for them; so We leave those who do not hope for meeting Us, i.e., do not believe in our meeting and in what We have of bliss and hellfire, in their rebellion, in their disbelief, wrongdoing, evil and corruption, wandering bewildered, unable to find a direction or a way out of the misguidance and blindness they are in.

This is what the first verse [11] indicates. As for the second verse [12], it contains the statement of a truth: that the human being who lives in the darkness of disbelief and has not been illumined by the light of faith, when harm touches him—sickness, poverty, or anything that harms—calls upon his Lord immediately, lying on his side, sitting, or standing, saying, "O my Lord, O my Lord." Then when God answers him and removes the harm he had, he passes on as though no sickness had touched him and he had never called upon Him, and he continues in his disbelief, wrongdoing and error. And His words: ﴿Thus it was made attractive to the transgressors what they used to do﴾, i.e., just as the disbelieving human being quickly forgets his Lord whom he called upon and who relieved his affliction, so too is the state of the transgressors in wrongdoing and evil; they see what they are upon as justice and good, and therefore they continue in their wrongdoing, evil and corruption. This is what His words ﴿Thus it was made attractive to the transgressors what they used to do﴾ indicate.

And His words in the third verse: ﴿And We destroyed the generations before you when they did wrong﴾. This is an address to the people of Mecca, informing them, warning them, that He carries out His custom concerning them: He destroyed the people of the generations before them when they did wrong, i.e., they associated partners with God, and their messengers came to them with clear proofs, i.e., signs and arguments, but they refused to believe because of the polytheism and sins to which they had become accustomed; so He destroyed them, like 'Ad, Thamud, and the people of Madyan. And His words ﴿Thus do We recompense the criminal people﴾, i.e., by a similar recompense, a general destruction, We recompense the criminal people at every time and place if they do not believe and become upright.

And His words in the verse: ﴿Then We made you successors in the earth after them, that We might see how you would act﴾, i.e., He says to the polytheist Arabs of Mecca and others: Then We made you successors in the earth after the destruction of those before you, that We might see how you act. If your deeds are good, We will recompense you for them, and if they are evil, We will recompense you for them. This is Our custom with Our servants, and God is not unaware of what the wrongdoers do.

Guidance from the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- Manifestations of God's mercy toward His servants: had He hastened for them the punishment they seek, as He hastens good for them when they ask for it, He would have destroyed them and decreed their death.

2- Sinners disobey God and disbelievers disbelieve in Him, and He leaves them in their falsehood and evil, not hastening punishment for them, perhaps they will return.

3- Clarification that the disbelieving human being recognizes God in hardship, calls upon Him and humbles himself before Him; but when He saves him, he returns to disbelief in Him as though he had never known Him.

4- The continued excess of the polytheists in disbelief, evil and corruption is made attractive to them according to God's custom; their example is that of the disbeliever who calls upon Him in hardship and forgets in ease.

5- God's warning to the people of crime of swift or deferred punishment if they do not repent.

6- All people, individually and collectively, are given respite, are observed in their deeds and conduct, and will certainly be recompensed for their deeds, good and evil.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 10, verses 11–14:

Explanation of the words:

Al-sharr (evil): everything that causes harm to the intellect, the body, wealth or offspring; al-khayr (good) is its opposite: that which brings benefit to the body, wealth or offspring.

La-qudiya ilayhim ajalahum (Had He hastened for them their term): they would have been destroyed and died.

Fa-nadharu (So We leave): i.e., We abandon.

Fi tughyanihim ya'mahun (in their rebellion, wandering blindly): i.e., in their wrongdoing and disbelief they wander back and forth, unable to come out of it, like the blind.

Al-durr (affliction): sickness and everything that harms the body, wealth or offspring.

Marra ka'an lam yad'unā (he passes on as though he had never called upon Us): he continues in his disbelief and falsehood as though he had never been the one who called upon Us to remove his affliction.

Kadhalika zuyyina (Thus it was made attractive): like that forgetting, which is swift after he had called for its removal, the wrongdoing and evil were made attractive to the transgressors (al-musrifin) in their excess.

Al-qurun (the generations): i.e., the people of the generations.

Bil-bayyinat (with clear proofs): with the arguments and signs of the truth of their message.

Khala'if (successors): i.e., for you, whom you succeed after their destruction.

Meaning of the verses:

During the period in which this Meccan surah was being revealed, the polytheists of Mecca were in great agitation and turmoil, to the extent that they demanded that punishment be sent down upon them. God, exalted is He, mentioned this about them in more than one verse of His Book, among them: ﴿They ask for the punishment to hasten; and had there not been an appointed term, the punishment would have come upon them﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 53], and in this matter the words of God were revealed: ﴿And if God were to hasten for people the evil﴾, i.e., upon their asking Him for it, or their doing what calls for it, as He hastens good for them, ﴿He would surely have decreed for them their term﴾, i.e., they would have been destroyed with a general destruction and their term in this life would have ended. And His words: ﴿So We leave those who do not expect meeting Us in their rebellion, wandering blindly﴾, i.e., We did not hasten punishment for them; so We leave those who do not hope for meeting Us, i.e., do not believe in our meeting and in what We have of bliss and hellfire, in their rebellion, in their disbelief, wrongdoing, evil and corruption, wandering bewildered, unable to find a direction or a way out of the misguidance and blindness they are in.

This is what the first verse [11] indicates. As for the second verse [12], it contains the statement of a truth: that the human being who lives in the darkness of disbelief and has not been illumined by the light of faith, when harm touches him—sickness, poverty, or anything that harms—calls upon his Lord immediately, lying on his side, sitting, or standing, saying, "O my Lord, O my Lord." Then when God answers him and removes the harm he had, he passes on as though no sickness had touched him and he had never called upon Him, and he continues in his disbelief, wrongdoing and error. And His words: ﴿Thus it was made attractive to the transgressors what they used to do﴾, i.e., just as the disbelieving human being quickly forgets his Lord whom he called upon and who relieved his affliction, so too is the state of the transgressors in wrongdoing and evil; they see what they are upon as justice and good, and therefore they continue in their wrongdoing, evil and corruption. This is what His words ﴿Thus it was made attractive to the transgressors what they used to do﴾ indicate.

And His words in the third verse: ﴿And We destroyed the generations before you when they did wrong﴾. This is an address to the people of Mecca, informing them, warning them, that He carries out His custom concerning them: He destroyed the people of the generations before them when they did wrong, i.e., they associated partners with God, and their messengers came to them with clear proofs, i.e., signs and arguments, but they refused to believe because of the polytheism and sins to which they had become accustomed; so He destroyed them, like 'Ad, Thamud, and the people of Madyan. And His words ﴿Thus do We recompense the criminal people﴾, i.e., by a similar recompense, a general destruction, We recompense the criminal people at every time and place if they do not believe and become upright.

And His words in the verse: ﴿Then We made you successors in the earth after them, that We might see how you would act﴾, i.e., He says to the polytheist Arabs of Mecca and others: Then We made you successors in the earth after the destruction of those before you, that We might see how you act. If your deeds are good, We will recompense you for them, and if they are evil, We will recompense you for them. This is Our custom with Our servants, and God is not unaware of what the wrongdoers do.

Guidance from the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- Manifestations of God's mercy toward His servants: had He hastened for them the punishment they seek, as He hastens good for them when they ask for it, He would have destroyed them and decreed their death.

2- Sinners disobey God and disbelievers disbelieve in Him, and He leaves them in their falsehood and evil, not hastening punishment for them, perhaps they will return.

3- Clarification that the disbelieving human being recognizes God in hardship, calls upon Him and humbles himself before Him; but when He saves him, he returns to disbelief in Him as though he had never known Him.

4- The continued excess of the polytheists in disbelief, evil and corruption is made attractive to them according to God's custom; their example is that of the disbeliever who calls upon Him in hardship and forgets in ease.

5- God's warning to the people of crime of swift or deferred punishment if they do not repent.

6- All people, individually and collectively, are given respite, are observed in their deeds and conduct, and will certainly be recompensed for their deeds, good and evil.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 10, verses 15–18:

Explanation of the words:

"Those who do not hope for meeting Us" (لا يرجون لقاءنا): i.e., they do not believe in resurrection (al-ba'th) and the Last Abode.

"Of my own accord" (من تلقاء نفسي): i.e., from myself.

"Nor would He have made you aware of it" (ولا أدراكم به): i.e., nor would I have informed you of it.

"A lifetime before it" (عمراً من قبله): i.e., forty years before I was inspired.

"The criminals" (المجرمون): those who corrupt themselves through polytheism (shirk) and sins.

"What does not harm them" (ما لا يضرهم): i.e., if they do not worship Him.

"Nor benefit them" (وما لا ينفعهم): i.e., if they do worship Him.

"Do you inform God" (أتنبئون): i.e., do you teach God and tell Him?

"Glory be to Him" (سبحانه): i.e., exalted above (tanzih).

"Of what they associate" (عما يشركون): i.e., with Him, such as idols.

Explanation of the verses:

The context continues to establish the three principles of the fundamentals of religion (usul al-din): monotheism (al-tawhid), revelation (al-wahy), and resurrection (al-ba'th). His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿And when Our verses are recited to them﴾, i.e., when the verses of Allah, mighty and majestic, are recited to them, ﴿those who do not hope for meeting Us said﴾, and they are the deniers of resurrection, since through it the meeting with Allah Most High for reckoning and recompense takes place. ﴿Bring a Qur'an other than this﴾, i.e., one that is free of any fault regarding our gods and of disparagement of them. Or change it, but replace its words with what does not offend us; put in place of a verse that contains what offends us another verse that contains no offense to us. Their saying this is either by way of challenge or mockery and derision. But Allah Most High taught His Messenger the manner of replying to them, based on the apparent meaning of their words, so He said to him: ﴿Say: It is not for me to change it of my own accord﴾, i.e., it is by no means possible for me to change it of my own accord, because I am the servant and messenger of Allah; I follow only what is revealed to me. ﴿Indeed, I fear, if I disobey my Lord, the punishment of a great day﴾, i.e., the punishment of the Day of Resurrection, by changing His speech. And His saying: ﴿Say: Had Allah willed, I would not have recited it to you, nor would He have made you aware of it﴾, i.e., say to them in reply to their demand: If Allah had willed that I not recite it to you, I would not have recited it to you, nor would He have made you aware of it through me; the matter is His, and I do not disobey Him. And to show you the truth of what I say: I dwelt among you a lifetime, i.e., forty years, before I brought it to you. ﴿Will you not then use your reason?﴾: [i.e., understand] the meaning of what I say to you and what proofs I mention to you?

This is what the first and second verses [15–16] indicate. As for the third verse, it contains a condemnation of the criminals who lie against Allah Most High by ascribing partners to Him and deny His signs and reject them. Allah Most High says: ﴿So who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against Allah or denies His signs?﴾, i.e., no one is more unjust. ﴿Or denies His signs﴾ after they have come to him, i.e., no one is more unjust than the two. His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿Indeed, the criminals will not succeed﴾ indicates first that those mentioned are criminals, and that they will not succeed, their case being that of all criminals. And if they do not succeed, they have lost and suffered loss. As for His saying in the fourth verse, ﴿They worship other than Allah what neither harms them nor benefits them﴾, i.e., the idols, ﴿and they say, "These are our intercessors with Allah."﴾ In this they are liars and fabricators. Therefore Allah commanded that He reply to them with His saying: ﴿Say: Do you inform Allah of what He does not know in the heavens or on the earth?﴾ For if there were someone who could intercede with Him, He would know of them and would have informed of them; so why the lying against Allah and fabricating about Him? Then Allah Most High declared Himself exalted above associating partners with Him and having partners: ﴿Glory be to Him, and high is He above what they associate.﴾

Guidance of the verses

From the guidance of these verses:

1- Among calling to Allah Most High is reciting His Qur'anic verses to people, as reminder and instruction.

2- Clarification of the obstinacy, denial and arrogance of the polytheists.

3- The Prophet ﷺ lived forty years in which he was not known for any learning or knowledge, then he emerged excelling in some sciences and knowledge, surpassing and exceeding everyone; this is a definite proof that he is a prophet to whom revelation is sent.

4- There is no one more unjust than either of two men: one who lies against Allah Most High, and another who denies Allah Most High.

5- Refutation of the claim of the polytheists that their gods will intercede for them with Allah on the Day of Resurrection.

6- Explanation of the reason the polytheists worship their gods, which is their hope for their intercession on their behalf.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 10, verses 19–20:

Explanation of the words:

Ummah wahidah (a single community): i.e., upon one religion, which is Islam.

Fakhtalafu (they differed): i.e., they split up, so that some remained upon monotheism and some upon polytheism (shirk).

Kalimah sabaqat (a word that had preceded): regarding leaving them to reach their appointed terms and recompensing them on the Day of Resurrection.

Ayah (a sign): an extraordinary sign, like the she-camel of Salih, peace be upon him.

Innama al-ghayb lillah (the unseen belongs only to Allah): i.e., the knowledge of when the sign will come from the unseen belongs to Allah alone. Neither I nor you know it. So wait, indeed I am with you among those who wait.

The meaning of the two verses:

He, the Exalted, informs His Messenger of a historical fact whose knowledge helps in patience and endurance. He says: ﴿Mankind was but one community﴾, i.e., in a former time, mankind was one community upon the religion of monotheism, the religion of the natural disposition (fitrah). Then the devils of jinn and mankind introduced innovations, desires and shirk among them, so they differed: some of them remained steadfast in faith and monotheism, and some of them disbelieved through shirk and misguidance. And His saying, the Exalted, ﴿And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord﴾, which is that He does not hasten punishment upon nations and individuals for their disbelief, but rather postpones them to their appointed terms in order to recompense them in the abode of recompense with the punishment of the Fire on the Day of Resurrection. Had it not been for His word, which is ﴿I will surely fill Hell with you and those who follow you among them, all together﴾ [Sad: 85], He would have hastened punishment for them. Thus He judged between them, destroying the disbeliever and saving the believer.

This is what the first verse [19] indicates. As for the second verse [20], He, the Exalted, informs about the polytheists that they said: ﴿Why has not a sign been sent down to him from his Lord?﴾ i.e., why was an extraordinary sign not sent down upon Muhammad from his Lord, so that we might know and infer from it that he is the Messenger of Allah? They may have meant by the sign a punishment, so Allah commanded His Messenger to respond to them by saying: ﴿The unseen belongs only to Allah﴾. He alone knows when the punishment will come to you. So ﴿wait, indeed I am with you among those who wait﴾. The period of waiting did not last long, and the punishment descended upon them at Badr, so their leaders and the greatest of the mockers perished.

Guidance from the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- The original state is monotheism, and shirk is an accidental development.

2- It is evil and shirk that cause disagreement in the community and division within it, whereas monotheism and goodness do not result in disagreement, war or division.

3- Explanation of the reason why the people of injustice and shirk continue to wrong and corrupt until their appointed terms.

4- All of the unseen belongs to Allah; no one knows the unseen except Allah, and whomever Allah teaches some of it. This is specific to the messengers, in order to establish proof against their nations.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 10, verses 21–23:

Explanation of the words:

Rahmah (mercy): i.e., rain after drought, or health after sickness, or wealth after poverty.

Darra' (adversity): a state of harm through sickness, barrenness, or poverty.

Makr fi ayatina (scheming against Our signs): i.e., mockery of them and denial.

Inna rusulana (indeed Our messengers): i.e., the guardian angels.

Yusayyirukum (He makes you travel): i.e., He enables you to travel by means of what is around you, such as vessels, and by the means He has made available to you.

Bi-rihin tayyibah (with a favorable wind): i.e., a wind suitable for the sailing of ships and in accordance with their purpose.

Rih 'asif (a violent wind): i.e., a severe wind that uproots trees and demolishes buildings.

Wa uhita bihim (and they were encompassed): i.e., destruction surrounded them from every direction.

Yabghuna bi-ghayr al-haqq (they act tyrannically without right): i.e., they wrong others, departing from truth and moderation.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues with the call to the people of Makkah to believe in the oneness of God, in His Messenger, and in the Last Day. He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And when We let the people taste mercy﴾, i.e., the disbelievers of Makkah, ﴿after adversity had touched them﴾, i.e., We let them taste the mercy, which is rain after drought, wealth after poverty, and health after sickness, and which is the adversity that had touched them for a period of time. They confront you with scheming against the signs of God, which is their mockery of them and their denial of them and of the one to whom they were revealed. As for His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Say: God is swifter in scheming﴾, i.e., say, O Our Messenger, to these scheming polytheists: God, mighty and majestic, is swifter in scheming than you, so He will show you the outcome of His scheme against you, which is your humiliation and disgrace in this world and your punishment in the Hereafter if you die in your disbelief. His saying ﴿Indeed Our messengers record what you scheme﴾ is a confirmation of what He has informed them of regarding God's scheme against them, since the recording by the angels of what they scheme is evidence of God's planning for them the harm with which He intends to repay them for their scheming.

This is what the first verse [21] contains. As for the second verse [22], it shows the polytheists their weakness, impotence, and need of God. Whoever is like this, how can he mock his Lord, ridicule His signs, and deny His Messenger? Indeed their state is astonishing. He, exalted is He, says: He is God, the One you scheme against in His signs, ﴿who enables you to travel on land and sea﴾, by what He has created for you of riding animals: camels, horses, and donkeys, and on the sea by what He has subjected to you of ships running upon the sea by His command. ﴿Until, when you are in ships and they sail with them﴾, i.e., the ships carry the polytheists ﴿with a favorable wind﴾, suitable for the sailing of ships, ﴿and they rejoice in it﴾, as is the custom of seafarers, who rejoice in a wind suitable to their safety from seasickness, unease, and turbulence. ﴿There comes to them a violent wind﴾, i.e., a strongly blowing wind by which the ships are tossed and their passengers fear drowning. ﴿And waves come to them from every place﴾, i.e., from every direction of the sea. The wave is the rise of the sea's water and its surging, like dust whirlwinds on land. ﴿And they think they are encompassed﴾, i.e., they become certain or nearly certain that they are about to perish. ﴿They call upon God, sincere to Him in religion﴾, i.e., they supplicate: "O Lord, O Lord, save us," and they make a vow, saying: ﴿If You save us from this﴾, i.e., from this destruction, ﴿we will surely be among the grateful﴾ to You, i.e., among those who obey and acknowledge Your favor upon us, affirming Your oneness by abandoning the deities worshipped alongside You, for Your worship alone, with no partner for You.

Then when He saves them from that hardship, they confront you with their transgression on earth without right, through polytheism, disbelief, wrongdoing, and corruption. They return to what they had been doing, and indeed they are liars. As for His saying, exalted is He, ﴿O mankind, your transgression is only against yourselves; [it is] the enjoyment of worldly life﴾, He informs them, saying: O mankind who transgress on earth without right, at whatever time you exist and in whatever place you are found, your transgression is only against yourselves, since its consequences return upon your own souls, for they are the ones that become sinful and corrupt in this world, and become deserving of God's punishment on the Day of Resurrection. His saying ﴿it is the enjoyment of worldly life﴾ means that this is the enjoyment of the worldly life, whether it is misery or happiness. ﴿Then to Us is your return﴾, i.e., not to anyone else, and that is after death on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿Then We will inform you of what you used to do﴾ of good and evil, and We will repay you with just recompense in the abode of recompense.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- Whoever schemes, God schemes against him, and God is swifter in scheming and greater in effect and harm.

2- Demonstration of man's weakness and poverty, and his need of God, mighty and majestic, for the preservation of his life and its continuance until his appointed term.

3- The servant's sincerity in supplication during hardship is a sign that monotheism is the origin and polytheism is an accident.

4- The early polytheists were in a better state than the ignorant of this nation, for they associated partners with God in ease and were sincere in hardship, whereas the ignorant among Muslims today associate partners with God constantly, in ease and hardship alike.

5- The transgression of a human being returns upon himself, like his scheming and breaking of covenant. In the hadith: "Three things return upon their doers: transgression, scheming, and breaking of covenant."

6- Affirmation of the principle of resurrection and recompense on the Day of Judgment.

As for His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Say: God is swifter in scheming﴾, i.e., say, O Our Messenger, to these scheming polytheists: God, mighty and majestic, is swifter in scheming than you, so He will show you the outcome of His scheme against you, which is your humiliation and disgrace in this world and your punishment in the Hereafter if you die in your disbelief. His saying ﴿Indeed Our messengers record what you scheme﴾ is a confirmation of what He has informed them of regarding God's scheme against them, since the recording by the angels of what they scheme is evidence of God's planning for them the harm with which He intends to repay them for their scheming.

This is what the first verse [21] contains. As for the second verse [22], it shows the polytheists their weakness, impotence, and need of God. Whoever is like this, how can he mock his Lord, ridicule His signs, and deny His Messenger? Indeed their state is astonishing. He, exalted is He, says: He is God, the One you scheme against in His signs, ﴿who enables you to travel on land and sea﴾, by what He has created for you of riding animals: camels, horses, and donkeys, and on the sea by what He has subjected to you of ships running upon the sea by His command. ﴿Until, when you are in ships and they sail with them﴾, i.e., the ships carry the polytheists ﴿with a favorable wind﴾, suitable for the sailing of ships, ﴿and they rejoice in it﴾, as is the custom of seafarers, who rejoice in a wind suitable to their safety from seasickness, unease, and turbulence. ﴿There comes to them a violent wind﴾, i.e., a strongly blowing wind by which the ships are tossed and their passengers fear drowning. ﴿And waves come to them from every place﴾, i.e., from every direction of the sea. The wave is the rise of the sea's water and its surging, like dust whirlwinds on land. ﴿And they think they are encompassed﴾, i.e., they become certain or nearly certain that they are about to perish. ﴿They call upon God, sincere to Him in religion﴾, i.e., they supplicate: "O Lord, O Lord, save us," and they make a vow, saying: ﴿If You save us from this﴾, i.e., from this destruction, ﴿we will surely be among the grateful﴾ to You, i.e., among those who obey and acknowledge Your favor upon us, affirming Your oneness by abandoning the deities worshipped alongside You, for Your worship alone, with no partner for You.

Then when He saves them from that hardship, they confront you with their transgression on earth without right, through polytheism, disbelief, wrongdoing, and corruption. They return to what they had been doing, and indeed they are liars. As for His saying, exalted is He, ﴿O mankind, your transgression is only against yourselves; [it is] the enjoyment of worldly life﴾, He informs them, saying: O mankind who transgress on earth without right, at whatever time you exist and in whatever place you are found, your transgression is only against yourselves, since its consequences return upon your own souls, for they are the ones that become sinful and corrupt in this world, and become deserving of God's punishment on the Day of Resurrection. His saying ﴿it is the enjoyment of worldly life﴾ means that this is the enjoyment of the worldly life, whether it is misery or happiness. ﴿Then to Us is your return﴾, i.e., not to anyone else, and that is after death on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿Then We will inform you of what you used to do﴾ of good and evil, and We will repay you with just recompense in the abode of recompense.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- Whoever schemes, God schemes against him, and God is swifter in scheming and greater in effect and harm.

2- Demonstration of man's weakness and poverty, and his need of God, mighty and majestic, for the preservation of his life and its continuance until his appointed term.

3- The servant's sincerity in supplication during hardship is a sign that monotheism is the origin and polytheism is an accident.

4- The early polytheists were in a better state than the ignorant of this nation, for they associated partners with God in ease and were sincere in hardship, whereas the ignorant among Muslims today associate partners with God constantly, in ease and hardship alike.

5- The transgression of a human being returns upon himself, like his scheming and breaking of covenant. In the hadith: "Three things return upon their doers: transgression, scheming, and breaking of covenant."

6- Affirmation of the principle of resurrection and recompense on the Day of Judgment.

Explanation of the words:

Like the life of this world: that is, its characteristic, which fits it and matches it.

Water: that is, rain.

Then mixed with it: that is, because of it the plants of the earth became intertwined with one another.

Of what men eat: such as wheat, the rest of the grains, fruits and vegetables.

And livestock: that is, of pasture and herbage, as is customary; though animals are sometimes fed barley.

Its adornment: that is, its freshness and brightness.

And is beautified: that is, it is adorned with flowers.

And its people think they have power over it: that is, they are able to gather its agricultural produce.

Our command comes upon it: that is, Our decree to destroy it and bring it to ruin as a punishment for its people.

Mown down: that is, as if it had been reaped with a sickle, with nothing standing in it.

As if it had not flourished yesterday: that is, as if it had not existed, flourishing yesterday.

We detail the signs: that is, We make them clear.

And Allah calls to the Abode of Peace: the Abode of Peace is Paradise, to which Allah invites His servants so that they prepare themselves for entering it, which is faith, righteous deeds, and abandoning shirk and sins.

The meaning of the two verses:

The noble context continues to present the divine guidance to people, so that they may be guided. In this verse, the Exalted gives an example of the life of this world, over which the heedless scramble and for which they sell their Hereafter, lying and wronging others for its sake. Its likeness, in its brightness that deceives those who are enamoured of it and its beauty that beguiles, is like water sent down from the heavens, mixing with it the plants of the earth, so they are watered by it, grow, flourish, bear leaves and fruit, and its people rejoice in it, and they come to think that they will benefit from it and gain by it. Then suddenly, by God's decree, a calamity comes upon it at an hour of night or day, and it becomes mown down, with nothing left standing upon its stalk, dry stubble scattered by the winds, as if it had not been flourishing yesterday, that is, as if it had not existed, standing and thriving in its place yesterday. The command of Allah came upon it because its people were wrongdoers, so He punished them with a calamity that ruined their crops, and they became despairing and grieving. This is the ideal image of the life of this world. Will the heedless not take heed, or will the sleepers not awaken from their state like mine?

As for His saying in the second verse [25]: ﴿And Allah calls to the Abode of Peace﴾, that is, by abandoning shirk and sins and turning to obedience and righteous deeds. The Abode of Peace is Paradise, for it is free from turbidity and disturbance: there is no sickness, no decrepitude, no death and no sorrow. The callers to misguidance call to this world, whose form and end is that it is an abode of turbidity, disturbance, anxiety and grief. So which of the two calls will be answered? ﴿And He guides whomever He wills to a straight path﴾. So let one seek His guidance sincerely, for none guides except Him. The straight path is Islam, the road to Paradise and the ladder to reach it. May Allah grant us to walk upon it and remain steadfast upon it.

Guidance from the two verses:

1- Clarifying the true picture of the life of this world in its freshness and its swift passing.

2- Warning against being deceived by this world and inclining to it.

3- Warning against sins, for they are the cause of misery and the removal of blessings.

4- The virtue of reflection and of those who reflect.

5- Allah's grace upon His servants and His mercy toward them, in that He calls them to His abode, honouring them and bestowing favour upon them.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 10, verses 26–30:

Explanation of the words:

Al-husna wa ziyadah (the best reward and an increase): al-husna is Paradise, and the ziyadah (increase) is gazing upon the Noble Face of Allah.

Wa la yarhaqu wujuhahum: that is, it will not cover their faces.

Qatar: a dust of gloom and sorrow.

Al-sayyi'at (the evil deeds): plural of sayyi'ah, that which harms the soul, namely the sins of shirk (associating partners with Allah) and acts of disobedience.

Makanakum (stay in your place): that is, remain in your places and do not leave them.

Fa-zayyalna baynahum: We separated them.

Hunalika: that is, there.

Tabluu kullu nafs: that is, tests.

Ma aslafat: that is, what it has sent forward.

Wa dalla 'anhum ma kanu yaftaruna: that is, what they used to fabricate and lie about has vanished from them.

Meaning of the verses:

After Allah, the Exalted, mentioned in the previous verse that He calls to the Abode of Peace, He mentioned the reward of those who accepted the call and of those who did not. He said: "For those who did good, [and] believed and worshipped Allah in the manner He prescribed, and affirmed His unity in His worship, lordship, names and attributes, their reward is al-husna, which is Paradise, and an increase, which is gazing upon His Noble Face in the Abode of Peace. And when they are raised, no dust or humiliation will cover their faces, as happens to those who did not answer the call of Allah." He confirmed their reward and clarified it by saying: ﴿Those are the companions of the Garden; they will abide therein eternally.﴾ He then mentioned the reward of those who turned away from the call and rejected it, persisting in disbelief, shirk and disobedience, saying: ﴿But those who have earned evil deeds - the recompense of an evil deed is an equivalent thereof.﴾ Those who earned the evil deeds of shirk and sins, which harmed their souls, corrupting and defiling them, their reward is Hell, and humiliation will overtake them on the plains of the Resurrection, and they will have no protector from Allah to shield them from the punishment of Allah. It is as if their faces were covered with pieces of the darkest night, because of their blackness. His saying, ﴿Those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally,﴾ confirms their destiny, may Allah protect us, which is constant residence in the Fire and no exit from it, for they abide in it forever.

These are the matters indicated by the first [26] and second [27] verses. As for the third, fourth and fifth verses, they contain a brief presentation of the gathering of people on the Day of Resurrection, and the purpose of this is to establish the creed of belief in the Last Day. He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And [mention] the Day We will gather them all together.﴾ That is, on the plains of the Resurrection. ﴿Then We will say to those who associated others with Allah: "Stay in your place, you and your partners."﴾ That is, those you took as gods and worshipped besides Us. ﴿Then We will separate them﴾, meaning Allah, the Exalted, will divide them, which is the meaning of His saying ﴿and We will separate them.﴾ There is no doubt that they will say, "Our Lord, these are our partners whom we used to call upon besides You." Therefore, Allah, the Exalted, mentioned their reply to them in His saying: ﴿And their partners will say, "You did not worship us."﴾ That is, because we did not hear you, nor see you, nor did we command you to worship us. This is the statement of everyone who was worshipped besides Allah from all the various kinds. ﴿So Allah is sufficient as a witness between us and you; we were certainly unaware of your worship.﴾ That is, by Allah, we were not at all aware of your worship in any way. Allah said: ﴿There, every soul will test what it has sent before﴾ - that is, in that dreadful situation, it will experience what it sent forward in its worldly life and recognise whether it was harmful or beneficial to it. ﴿And they will be returned to Allah, their true Master, and lost from them will be what they used to fabricate.﴾ Thus they will find themselves before their Master, the Owner of their affairs, their true God, whom they had long disbelieved in, denied, and rejected His signs and messengers. "Lost" means that what they used to invent of falsehoods, lies and fabrications, from those idols they named gods and worshipped, has vanished from them. They will regret on a day when regret will not benefit, and Allah will repay them with what they had not reckoned.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Clarification of the virtue of good deeds and what follows them of attaining the best reward.

2- Clarification of the evil of evil deeds and what they bring of regret, remorse and the loss they entail.

3- Establishing the belief in resurrection and recompense through a true and clear presentation.

4- Disavowal by what is worshipped besides Allah of its worshippers; whether the object of worship is an angel, a human, a jinn, a tree or a stone, all will disown their worshippers, and Allah takes them as witnesses against them.

5- On the plains of the Resurrection, every soul will know what it presented and what it delayed, and will test what it sent forward, so it will recognise it; but how can it benefit from what it recognises?

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 10, verses 26–30:

Wa la yarhaqu wujuhahum: that is, it will not cover their faces.

Qatar: a dust of gloom and sorrow.

Al-sayyi'at (the evil deeds): plural of sayyi'ah, that which harms the soul, namely the sins of shirk (associating partners with Allah) and acts of disobedience.

Makanakum (stay in your place): that is, remain in your places and do not leave them.

Fa-zayyalna baynahum: We separated them.

Hunalika: that is, there.

Tabluu kullu nafs: that is, tests.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 10, verses 31–33:

Explanation of the words:

"من السماء" (min as-samā'): i.e., with rain and downpour.

"والأرض" (wal-arḍ): i.e., with plants, grains and fruits.

"أمَّن يملك السمع والأبصار" (Amman yamlik as-sam'a wal-abṣār): i.e., who controls your hearing and your sight. If He wills, He leaves them to you; if He wills, He takes them away from you.

"ومن يخرج الحي من الميت" (wa man yukhrij al-ḥayy min al-mayyit): i.e., He brings a living body out of a dead body, and the reverse likewise.

"ومن يدبر الأمر" (wa man yudabbir al-amr): i.e., the affair of all creatures: life and death, health and sickness, giving and withholding.

"أفلا تتقون" (afalā tattaqūn): i.e., fear God, so do not associate anything with Him and do not disobey His command and prohibition.

"فأنى تصرفون" (fa-anná tuṣrafūn): i.e., how are you turned away from the truth after knowing it? The truth is that there is no god but Allah.

"حقت" (ḥaqqat): i.e., became binding.

"أنهم لا يؤمنون" (annahum lā yu'minūn): this is because they have reached a limit at which they are no longer able to repent at all.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues to establish the creed of Tawhid. Allah, the Exalted, says to His Messenger: ﴿Say﴾, O Our Messenger, to those polytheists, asking them: ﴿"Who provides for you from the heaven and the earth?"﴾ by sending down rain and by causing grains, fruits, vegetables and produce to grow, which you are provided with. And say to them: ﴿"Who controls hearing and sight?"﴾ that is, your hearing and your sight, such that if He wills, He leaves them to you and lets you enjoy them, and if He wills, He takes them from you and deprives you of them, so you become blind who do not see and deaf who do not hear. ﴿"And who brings the living out of the dead"﴾ like a chick out of an egg, ﴿"and brings the dead out of the living"﴾ like an egg out of a hen, and a palm tree out of a date stone, and a date stone out of a palm tree. ﴿"And who manages the affair"﴾ in the heavens and the earth, such as the alternation of night and day and the sending down of rains, and life and death, wealth and poverty, war and peace, health and sickness, and other manifestations of Divine management in the universe. ﴿They will say, "Allah,"﴾ since they have no answer but this. Then, since Allah is the One who does this and has power over it apart from others, how is He not feared, the Mighty and Majestic, by His being declared one and by not associating anything with Him? So why do you not fear Him?

And the saying of the Exalted: ﴿"So that is Allah, your Lord"﴾ i.e., that One who provides for you from the heaven and the earth, brings the living out of the dead, brings the dead out of the living, and manages the affair, is your true Lord, besides whom you have no lord. Then ﴿"what is there after the truth but error? So how are you turned away?"﴾ i.e., how are they turned away from the truth after knowing it, toward error? It is a matter that calls for astonishment and wonder!

And the saying of the Exalted: ﴿"Thus has the word of your Lord come to pass against those who defied, that they do not believe"﴾ i.e., like that turning away which the polytheists turn away from the truth after knowing it, toward error, just as the word of your Lord has come to pass, namely that Allah does not guide the defiant people, so they are not guided. This is because when a servant goes to extremes in evil and corruption through persistence and continuing in it, he reaches a limit from which he cannot return or come out in any way, so he perishes in his defiance, and the word of punishment comes due upon him, which is ﴿"I will surely fill Hell with you and with those among them who follow you, all together"﴾ [Sad: 85].

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- The polytheists of the Arabs associated partners with Allah in worship, while affirming His unity in lordship.

2- It does not benefit a servant to affirm His unity in lordship while associating partners with Him in worship.

3- There is nothing after the truth but error; there is no intermediate between them, so whoever is not upon the truth is upon error.

4- Going to extremes in evil and corruption becomes second nature to its doer, so he does not leave it until he perishes by it.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 10, verses 34–36:

Explanation of the words:

"من شركائكم" (min shuraka'ikum): plural of "shareek" (partner), i.e. those whom they associated with God in worship.

"من يبدأ الخلق" (man yabda'u al-khalq): i.e., who originates the creation of man and animals in the first place; that is the beginning (bad') of their creation.

"فأنى تؤفكون" (fa-anna tu'fakun): i.e., how are you turned away from the truth after knowing it?

"أمَّن لا يَهِدِّي" (amman la yahiddi): i.e., one who does not find guidance.

"كيف تحكمون" (kayfa tahkumun): i.e., this corrupt judgment you make, namely following one who is not valid to follow because he does not guide.

The meaning of the verses:

The discourse continues in the argument with the polytheists, to make the truth clear to them and call them to follow it. God says to His Messenger ﷺ: Say to these polytheists, ﴿Say: Is there any of your partners who originates creation and then repeats it?﴾ That is, is there among your deities that you worship anyone who originates the creation of a human from nothingness, then causes him to die, then brings him back? Their answer is well known: none exists. So how are you turned away, i.e., diverted from the truth after knowing it and acknowledging it? And say to them also, ﴿Say: Is there any of your partners who guides to the truth?﴾ That is, is there among your deities one who guides to the truth? The answer is: none exists, because they neither speak nor know. So say to them: God guides to the truth, i.e., through His Messenger, His revelation and His signs.

And say to them, ﴿Is he who guides to the truth more worthy to be followed, or he who does not find guidance unless he is guided?﴾ The answer is well known: the one who guides to the truth is more worthy to be followed than one who does not find guidance unless he is guided. So why do you not fear God, so that you would single Him out, believe in His Messenger and His Book, and be guided, and abandon your deities that do not guide to the truth? ﴿What is the matter with you?﴾ i.e., what proof have you established for abandoning the worship of God in favor of worshiping other than Him, these idols? ﴿How do you judge?﴾ i.e., what judgment is this that you pass, namely following one who does not guide and abandoning the worship of One who guides to the truth. And His saying, ﴿And most of them follow nothing but conjecture﴾, i.e., most of these polytheists follow in worshiping their idols nothing but conjecture; they have no certainty that these are truly deities deserving of worship. ﴿Indeed, conjecture avails not against the truth at all﴾, i.e., conjecture is not sufficient in place of knowledge and does not replace it in any way; what is required in belief is knowledge, not conjecture. And His saying, ﴿Indeed, God is Knowing of what they do﴾: this sentence carries a severe warning to them for their persistence in falsehood and their obstinacy against the truth, so He will recompense them with the requital appropriate to their wrongdoing and obstinacy.

Lessons from the verses:

1- Affirmation of monotheism by refuting the supposed deities, since their worshippers acknowledge that they do not originate creation nor restore it after death, and do not guide to the truth, whereas God originates creation, then restores it, and guides to the truth.

2- Refutation of corrupt rulings, not approving them, and the obligation to correct them.

3- Conjecture is not accepted in matters of belief; rather, certain knowledge is necessary in them.

4- Disapproval of speaking and acting upon conjecture, and in the hadith: "Beware of conjecture, for conjecture is the most false of speech."

"أمَّن لا يَهِدِّي" (amman la yahiddi): i.e., one who does not find guidance.

"كيف تحكمون" (kayfa tahkumun): i.e., this corrupt judgment you make, namely following one who is not valid to follow because he does not guide.

The meaning of the verses:

The discourse continues in the argument with the polytheists, to make the truth clear to them and call them to follow it. God says to His Messenger ﷺ: Say to these polytheists, ﴿Say: Is there any of your partners who originates creation and then repeats it?﴾ That is, is there among your deities that you worship anyone who originates the creation of a human from nothingness, then causes him to die, then brings him back? Their answer is well known: none exists. So how are you turned away, i.e., diverted from the truth after knowing it and acknowledging it? And say to them also, ﴿Say: Is there any of your partners who guides to the truth?﴾ That is, is there among your deities one who guides to the truth? The answer is: none exists, because they neither speak nor know. So say to them: God guides to the truth, i.e., through His Messenger, His revelation and His signs.

And say to them, ﴿Is he who guides to the truth more worthy to be followed, or he who does not find guidance unless he is guided?﴾ The answer is well known: the one who guides to the truth is more worthy to be followed than one who does not find guidance unless he is guided. So why do you not fear God, so that you would single Him out, believe in His Messenger and His Book, and be guided, and abandon your deities that do not guide to the truth? ﴿What is the matter with you?﴾ i.e., what proof have you established for abandoning the worship of God in favor of worshiping other than Him, these idols? ﴿How do you judge?﴾ i.e., what judgment is this that you pass, namely following one who does not guide and abandoning the worship of One who guides to the truth. And His saying, ﴿And most of them follow nothing but conjecture﴾, i.e., most of these polytheists follow in worshiping their idols nothing but conjecture; they have no certainty that these are truly deities deserving of worship. ﴿Indeed, conjecture avails not against the truth at all﴾, i.e., conjecture is not sufficient in place of knowledge and does not replace it in any way; what is required in belief is knowledge, not conjecture. And His saying, ﴿Indeed, God is Knowing of what they do﴾: this sentence carries a severe warning to them for their persistence in falsehood and their obstinacy against the truth, so He will recompense them with the requital appropriate to their wrongdoing and obstinacy.

Lessons from the verses:

1- Affirmation of monotheism by refuting the supposed deities, since their worshippers acknowledge that they do not originate creation nor restore it after death, and do not guide to the truth, whereas God originates creation, then restores it, and guides to the truth.

2- Refutation of corrupt rulings, not approving them, and the obligation to correct them.

3- Conjecture is not accepted in matters of belief; rather, certain knowledge is necessary in them.

4- Disapproval of speaking and acting upon conjecture, and in the hadith: "Beware of conjecture, for conjecture is the most false of speech."

**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 10, verses 37–39:**

**Explanation of the words:**

*An yuftara min dūni Allāh* (that it be fabricated apart from God): that is, a fabrication; i.e., this Qur'an is not a fabrication.

*Wa-tafṣīl al-kitāb* (and the detailed explanation of the Book): that is, the clarification of what God the Exalted has prescribed for this community, and what He has made lawful for it and what He has made unlawful.

*Am yaqūlūna iftarāhu* (or do they say, "He has invented it"): that is, he fabricated it from himself and invented it on his own.

*Bi-mā lam yuḥīṭū bi-ʿilmihi* (with what they have not encompassed in knowledge): that is, with what God the Exalted has threatened them with of punishment.

*Wa-lammā ya'tihim ta'wīluhu* (and its interpretation has not yet come to them): that is, and the outcome to which that threat of punishment will lead has not yet come to them.

*Kadhālika kadhdhaba alladhīna min qablihim* (likewise did those before them deny): that is, just as these people denied God's promise to them, those before them denied.

**Meaning of the verses:**

These verses establish the doctrine of revelation and affirm the prophethood of the Messenger ﷺ. God the Exalted says: ﴿And this Qur'an could not have been fabricated apart from God﴾, i.e., it is not within the nature of this great Qur'an that it be invented by anyone other than God the Exalted from among all His creatures. ﴿But it is a confirmation of what was before it﴾, i.e., it is the speech of God and His revelation, which He revealed to His Messenger and sent down as a confirmation of what came before it, namely the books that preceded its descent, the Torah and the Gospel. ﴿And a detailed explanation of the Book﴾ which God has prescribed for the community of Islam, of obligations, laws and rulings. The saying of God the Exalted ﴿there is no doubt in it﴾, i.e., there is no doubt that it is the revelation and speech of God, sent down from the Lord of the worlds. He is God, the Sustainer of creatures in their bodies, minds, morals and spirits; and it is among the requirements of His lordship to send down a Book containing an explanation of everything the servant needs for his upbringing and his physical, spiritual, intellectual and moral perfection.

God the Exalted says in the second verse [38]: ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"?﴾, i.e., rather, these polytheists and deniers say—and this is a statement of utmost frivolity and ugliness—"The Qur'an he has invented; Muhammad fabricated it, and it was not a revelation sent down to him." Say, O our Messenger, challenging them: bring a surah like it. Indeed, they are unable to do so, and thereby their claim is refuted. And say to them: call upon whoever you are able to obtain help from for bringing a surah like the surah of the Qur'an, if you are truthful in your claim that the Qur'an was not a revelation from God, but a fabrication invented by Muhammad, the Messenger of God ﷺ. The saying of God the Exalted ﴿Rather, they denied what they did not encompass in knowledge, and its interpretation had not yet come to them﴾, i.e., the matter is not that they were unable to perceive that the Qur'an is the speech of God; rather, the matter is that they denied what they had not encompassed in knowledge, namely God's threat of punishment against them, and its outcome had not yet come to them, since the threat's end-result is what they would have to face. Had they seen the punishment, they would not have denied. That is why God the Exalted says: ﴿Thus did those before them deny﴾, i.e., ﴿until they tasted Our might﴾ [al-An'am: 148], as in the verse of al-An'am. Here God the Exalted says: ﴿So look how was the end of the wrongdoers﴾. God has destroyed the wrongdoers: from the people of Noah by drowning, from the people of Hud by a violent wind, from the people of Salih by the blast, from the people of Shu'ayb by the earthquake, and from other nations by whatever kinds of punishment He willed. So these people, if they do not repent and persist in their denial, will surely suffer what befell others. ﴿And do not think that God is unaware of what the wrongdoers do﴾ [Ibrahim: 42].

**Guidance from the verses:**

1. Establishing the doctrine of revelation and affirming the prophethood of Muhammad ﷺ.

2. Among the proofs that the Qur'an is the speech of God is that it confirms the earlier books and does not contradict them, since both come from one source, God, the Lord of the worlds.

3. Among the Qur'an's proofs that it is the revelation of God is that God challenged the Arabs to produce a single surah equal to it in eloquence and rhetoric, and their inability to do so demonstrates its inimitability.

4. The polytheists' persistence in obstinacy and denial is due to their not yet having tasted the punishment God threatened them with; for had they tasted it, they would have believed, but faith would then not benefit them.
