Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 10, verses 40–44:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Among them are those who believe in it﴾: i.e., among the Makkan deniers of the Qur'an there are those who will believe in it in the future.

﴿Your Lord knows best the corrupters﴾: they are the callers to misguidance who corrupt minds and hearts. The sentence is a warning to them.

﴿And if they deny you﴾: i.e., they persist in denying you.

﴿Among them are those who listen to you﴾: i.e., when you recite the Qur'an.

﴿Among them are those who look at you﴾: i.e., they see and witness the signs of prophethood and the markers of your truthfulness, yet they are not guided to recognising that you are the Messenger of Allah, because Allah, exalted is He, has deprived them of that.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues to establish the prophethood of the Prophet ﷺ. Allah, exalted is He, says in addressing His Messenger, to console him and to make him patient regarding the non-belief of his people despite the clarity of the evidence and the strength of the proofs: ﴿And among them are those who believe in it﴾, i.e., in the Qur'an and in the Prophet as well, since belief in one entails belief in the other, ﴿and among them are those who do not believe in it﴾. This is a report of the unseen which came to pass exactly as Allah, exalted is He, had reported: a large number of the polytheists believed, and another number did not. His saying ﴿Your Lord knows best the corrupters﴾, i.e., those who do not believe, is also a warning to those who turn people away and bar them from faith and monotheism. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if they deny you﴾, i.e., they persist in their denial of you, so do not concern yourself with them and say: ﴿To me is my work and to you is your work. You are free of what I do, and I am free of what you do﴾. So if there is a worldly punishment, you will be spared from it and they will be destroyed by it.

His saying, exalted is He, in verse [42]: ﴿And among them are those who listen to you﴾, to your recitation of the Qur'an and to your speech when you call, command or forbid. Despite this, they do not understand and do not benefit from what they hear, and there is no blame on you for that, because you do not make the deaf hear, and these are deaf who do not hear. ﴿And among them are those who look at you﴾ with open eyes, seeing the signs of prophethood and the markers of messengership clear in your condition and your speech, yet they are not guided. There is no blame on you, for you do not guide the blind, even if they cannot see. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong people at all, but people wrong themselves﴾ is an explanation of the sunnah of Allah, exalted is He, regarding those who hear but do not benefit from their hearing, and see but do not benefit from what they see: whoever goes to excess in hatred and aversion to something becomes unable to benefit from what he hears from it or sees in it. Hence it is said: "Your love for a thing blinds you and deafens you." Likewise hatred. Just as persistence in evil and corruption for a period of time deprives its doer of repentance to good and righteousness. Hence Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong people at all, but people wrong themselves﴾.

Guidance from the verses:

1. The Qur'an's report of the unseen and its truthfulness in that.
2. Confirmation of the meaning of the verse ﴿For indeed, it is not the eyes that are blinded, but blinded are the hearts within the breasts﴾ [al-Hajj: 46].
3. Teaching the Messenger of Allah the method of argumentation (ḥijāj) and of refuting the polytheist opponents.
4. The negation of wrongdoing from Allah, exalted is He, and its affirmation of humans against themselves.

Explanation of the words:

"Yahshuruhum" (He will gather them): that is, We will resurrect them from their graves and gather them to the place of the judgment's decision.

"Ka'an lam yalbathu" (as though they had not remained): that is, in the world, alive in their homes and dead in their graves.

"Aw natawaffayanaka" (or We take you in death): that is, We cause you to die before that.

"Fa-idha ja'a rasuluhum" (when their messenger comes): that is, on the plains of the Resurrection.

"Bil-qist" (with justice): that is, with fairness.

"Mata hadha al-wa'd" (when is this promise): that is, the punishment on the Day of Resurrection.

The meaning of the verses:

The context continues to establish the doctrine of resurrection and recompense, so Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿And [mention] the Day He will gather them﴾, that is, remind them of the Day We gather them from their graves after resurrecting them alive, ﴿as if they had not remained﴾ in the world, alive in their homes and dead in their graves. ﴿except for an hour of the day, they will be recognizing one another﴾, that is, so that some of them may see others for an hour, and then the horror of the situation will come between them. The words of Allah, the Exalted, ﴿Those have certainly lost who denied the meeting with Allah, and they were not guided﴾ inform that those who denied the Last Resurrection, the reckoning, and the otherworldly recompense, and therefore did not hope for the meeting with Allah so as to act in accordance with His pleasure and abandon His displeasure, have indeed lost themselves and their families in Hell on that Day. His words, the Exalted, ﴿Then Allah is Witness over what they do﴾ are an affirmation and confirmation of their recompense on the Day of Resurrection, because Allah's knowledge of their deeds and His witnessing over them is sufficient to make their punishment obligatory. His words, the Exalted, ﴿And for every nation is a messenger. So when their messenger comes, the matter will be judged between them with justice, and they will not be wronged﴾, that is: for every nation among the nations there is a messenger sent to it who conveyed to it, so whoever obeyed obeyed and whoever disobeyed disobeyed. When their messenger comes on the plains of the Resurrection, judgment is made between them, that is, they are reckoned with or recompensed with justice, that is, with fairness, and they will not be wronged, neither by diminishing the good deeds of the doers of good nor by increasing the evil deeds of the evildoers. **Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 10, verses 49–53**

**Explanation of the words:**

*"Lanafsi darran"* (لنفسي ضراً): I do not have the power to remove harm if God, exalted is He, does not help me.

*"Wa la naf'an"* (ولا نفعاً): I do not have the power to bring benefit to myself if God does not will it for me.

*"Likulli ummatin ajal"* (لكل أمة أجل): for every community there is a set time for its destruction.

*"Fa la yasta'khirun sa'ah"* (فلا يستأخرون ساعة): they cannot delay from that term by a single hour.

*"Wa la yastaqdimun"* (ولا يستقدمون): nor can they advance upon it by an hour.

*"Qul ara'aytum"* (قل أرأيتم): say to them, "Tell me."

*"Thumma idha ma waqa'"* (أثم إذا ما وقع): when it befalls, i.e., when the punishment arrives.

*"Adhab al-khuld"* (عذاب الخلد): the punishment in which they will abide forever, never leaving it.

*"Wa yastanbi'unaka"* (ويستنبئونك): and they ask you for information.

*"Qul iyy"* (قل إي): say, "Yes."

*"Wa ma antum bi-mu'jizin"* (وما أنتم بمعجزين): you will not escape the punishment nor be saved from it.

**Meaning of the verses:**

The noble context continues in refuting the polytheists, who in the previous verses asked for the punishment, saying, ﴿When is this promise, if you are truthful?﴾ (Yunus 10:48), meaning the punishment. God therefore commanded His Messenger in these verses to say to them: I ﴿do not control for myself any harm﴾, meaning I do not control the removal of harm from myself, nor the bringing of benefit to myself, if God does not will that. How then could I know the unseen and know when the punishment will come to you, just as I cannot hasten it if God wills to delay it? Know also that for every nation there is a term, a specified time for its destruction and death, so they cannot delay from it for an hour, nor advance upon it by even a moment. Therefore there is no point in demanding that you be given the punishment.

Another matter: ﴿Tell me﴾, meaning inform me, if the punishment you are hastening comes upon you by night (*bayatan*) or by day, will you be able to bear it and withstand it? Then what is it you are hastening for, O criminals? You are hastening for a grave matter.

As for His saying, ﴿Only when it befalls will you believe in it?﴾, meaning: will you continue in denial and obstinacy, and then, when it befalls, believe in it? Will your belief benefit you on that day? It will be said to you in rebuke and reproach: now you believe in it, when you used to be hastening it.

As for His saying, ﴿Then it will be said to those who did wrong, "Taste the punishment of eternity. Are you recompensed except for what you used to earn?"﴾: God informs that when the criminals, who are those who wronged themselves through polytheism and sins, enter the Fire, they will be told, mockingly, to taste the punishment of eternity, meaning the everlasting punishment that does not perish or end. You are recompensed only for what you used to earn of polytheism and sins.

As for His saying, ﴿And they ask you, "Is it true?"﴾, meaning: the obstinate polytheists ask you, saying, "Is what you promise us of punishment on the Day of Resurrection true?" Answer them by saying, ﴿Yes, by my Lord, it is certainly true, and you cannot escape it﴾, meaning you cannot escape God nor outrun Him. Rather, He will surely compel you to the punishment, compelling you to it, and make you taste it as a painful, lasting punishment while you are humiliated.

**Guidance from the verses:**

1. No created being has power over harm to remove or benefit to bring, even for himself, let alone for others, except by God's permission and will. Those who rely on saints (*awliya'*) to bring them benefit or to ward off harm from them will be disappointed.

2. Terms are fixed; they neither advance nor delay. Therefore there is no point in the servant being fearful (*al-jubn*) on that account.

3. Faith and repentance do not benefit at the moment of seeing the punishment or the arrival of the Angel of Death.

4. It is permissible to swear by God when one wishes to emphasize a statement.

5. *Iyy* (إي) is a particle of affirmation, and it is always accompanied by an oath, as in *iyy wallahi* ("yes, by God") and *iyy wa-rabbi* ("yes, by my Lord").

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 10, verses 54–58:

Explanation of the words:

*Iftadat bihi* (لافتدت به): would have offered it as ransom for it.

*Wa-asarrū al-nadāmah* (وأسروا الندامة): they concealed it within themselves, [their] regret over abandoning faith and righteous deeds.

*Wa-qudiya baynahum bil-qist* (وقضي بينهم بالقسط): that is, Allah judged between them with justice.

*Wa'd Allah ḥaqq* (وعد الله حق): that is, what Allah promises them is certainly true.

*Mawʿizah min Rabbikum* (موعظة من ربكم): that is, an admonition from your Lord concerning truth and goodness, and concerning avoiding polytheism (shirk) and evil.

*Wa-hudā* (وهدى): that is, a clarification of the path of truth and goodness, distinguished from the path of falsehood and evil.

*Faḍl Allah wa-raḥmatuh* (فضل الله ورحمته): what He guided them to of faith, righteous deeds, and avoidance of polytheism and sins.

*Fa-bidhālika falyafraḥū* (فبذلك فليفرحوا): that is, with faith and righteous deeds after knowledge and God-consciousness (taqwa), let them rejoice and be glad.

*Huwa khayrun mimmā yajmaʿūn* (هو خير مما يجمعون): that is, better than wealth and perishable worldly goods.

Explanation of the verses:

The context continues to clarify that what Allah has promised the polytheists of punishment is coming without doubt if they do not believe, and that it is a punishment that cannot be endured. Allah says, ﴿And if every soul that had wronged [itself through polytheism and sins] had whatever is on earth, it would surely offer it for ransom﴾: that is, if it possessed everything on earth of wealth, both property and livestock, and it were accepted from it, it would offer it as ransom from the punishment, because of the severity of the punishment. Allah says, concerning the disbelievers who are in the place of gathering on the Day of Resurrection and who have seen the Fire, ﴿And they will conceal regret when they see the punishment﴾: that is, they will hide it within their breasts and not speak it, and it is their intense regret over not believing and not following the Messenger ﷺ. His saying, ﴿And they will be judged between with justice, and they will not be wronged﴾: that is, Allah the Exalted has judged, i.e., ruled, between the monotheists and the polytheists, the wrongdoers and the wronged, with justice, which is the divine justice, while they are not wronged by being held accountable for what they did not earn. His saying, ﴿Unquestionably, to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth﴾: that is, be alert and listen, O polytheists: indeed, to Allah belongs, in true ownership, whatever is in the heavens and the earth of all creatures, and no one shares with Him any of that ownership. He disposes of His dominion as He wills; He punishes and shows mercy, He makes wretched and makes happy, and none may object to Him. ﴿Unquestionably, the promise of Allah is true﴾: that is, be alert once more and listen: indeed the promise of Allah, meaning what He has promised you of punishment, is a established truth that will not fail. His saying, ﴿But most of them do not know﴾: for if they knew that the punishment is certainly coming and knew its magnitude, they would not have disbelieved in it. His saying, ﴿He gives life and causes death, and to Him you will be returned﴾: Allah the Exalted informs of Himself that He gives life and causes death, and whoever is able to give life and cause death is able to do everything. Among that is the bringing back to life of the disbelievers after their death, their gathering before Him, and their recompense for what they earned of evil and corruption. His saying, ﴿And to Him you will be returned﴾ establishes the principle of the final return.

After these affirmations of the three articles of faith—monotheism (tawhid), prophethood (nubuwwah), and resurrection and recompense (ba'th wal-jaza')—Allah the Exalted called out to Arabs and non-Arabs alike, saying: ﴿O mankind, there has certainly come to you an admonition from your Lord and a healing for what is in the breasts and guidance and mercy for the believers﴾. Each of these—the admonition, which is command and prohibition in the manner of encouragement and warning, and the healing, guidance, and mercy—the noble Qur'an has encompassed. It is as if He said: O mankind, among you are the ignorant, the defiant, the sick with polytheism and disbelief, the astray from the truth, and the one afflicted in body and soul. The Qur'an has come to you carrying all of that for you, so believe in it, follow the light it carries, seek its cure, and be guided by its light: you will be healed, and you will be perfected in intellect, character, and spirit, and you will be made happy in both lives together.

His saying, ﴿Say: "In the bounty of Allah and in His mercy—in that let them rejoice; it is better than what they accumulate"﴾: that is, convey [this], O our Messenger, commanding them to rejoice in Islam, its laws, the Qur'an and its sciences, for that is better than what they accumulate of the perishable goods of this world, and than what follows from it of evil consequences that cannot be borne or endured.

Lessons from the verses:

1. The magnitude of the punishment of the Day of Resurrection, to the extent that the disbeliever would wish to ransom himself from it with everything on earth.

2. Affirmation of the lordship of Allah over all creatures in the upper and lower worlds.

3. Praise of the virtue and greatness of the Qur'an for what it carries of admonition, guidance, mercy, and healing.

4. Rejoicing in the religion is recommended, and rejoicing in worldly things is disliked.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 10, verses 59–61:

Explanation of the words:

Ara'aytum (أرأيتم): i.e., tell me.

Ma anzala Allah lakum min rizq (ما أنزل الله لكم من رزق): i.e., that which Allah created for you of provision, such as the flesh of livestock.

A-Allahu adhina lakum (ءآلله أذن لكم): i.e., in prohibition, when you prohibited the baheera and the saiba, and in permission, when you made lawful carrion.

Yaftarun 'ala Allahi al-kadhib (يفترون على الله الكذب): i.e., they fabricate lies, forging them against Him and inventing them in their own minds.

Wa ma takunu fi sha'n (وما تكون في شأن): i.e., in a great matter.

Shuhudan idh tufidun fihi (شهوداً إذْ تفيضون فيه): i.e., you take up in speech or action concerning it.

Wa ma ya'zubu 'an rabbika (وما يعزب عن ربك): i.e., is hidden.

Min mithqal dharra (من مثقال ذرة): i.e., the weight of an atom, and the dharra is the smallest ant.

Illa fi kitabin mubin (إلا في كتاب مبين): i.e., the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz), and mubin means clear.

Meaning of the verses:

The context of the verses is the affirmation of revelation and the obligation upon the polytheist deniers of it to provide rational proof. Allah the Exalted said to His Messenger (ﷺ): Say to these polytheists, ﴿Say: Tell me, what provision Allah has sent down for you﴾, i.e., tell me about what Allah created for you of plants, food and tilth, and you made from it what is forbidden, such as the baheera and the saiba, the garments you forbid for circumambulation, and the tilth you dedicated to your gods, and what is lawful, such as carrion which you deem permissible. ﴿Has Allah permitted you?﴾ (in this legislation by revelation from Him) ﴿Or do you fabricate against Allah?﴾ If you say, "Allah has permitted us by revelation," then why do you deny revelation and call it a lie? And if you say, "There is no revelation, but we lie against Allah," then your position is then the worst position, for you fabricate lies against Allah. And Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And what will be the thought of those who fabricate lies against Allah on the Day of Resurrection?﴾ i.e., when they stand before Him, glorified and exalted, what do they think: will He forgive them and pardon them? No, rather they will be cursed and they will abide forever in the Fire. And His saying, ﴿Indeed, Allah is full of bounty toward mankind﴾ regarding His not hastening punishment for them while they lie against Him, associate others with Him, disobey Him and disobey His Messenger, ﴿but most of them do not give thanks﴾, and that is due to their ignorance and the corrupt upbringing among them; otherwise, the norm for a human being is to be thankful for the least kindness and the smallest favour.

And His saying, ﴿And you are not engaged in any affair, nor do you recite from it any portion of the Qur'an﴾, i.e., you, O our Messenger, are not in any of your important affairs, nor do you recite from the Qur'an any verse or verses concerning that affair, ﴿but We are witnesses over you﴾, i.e., present, ﴿when you are engaged in it﴾, i.e., at the time you take it up. And His saying, ﴿And not hidden from your Lord is an atom's weight within the earth or within the heaven, nor anything smaller than that or greater, but that it is in a clear record﴾: He, the Exalted, informs of the vastness of His knowledge and His encompassing of all His creatures, such that nothing is hidden from His knowledge, the weight of an atom, i.e., the weight of a dharra, which is the small ant, whether it is in the earth or in the heaven, and whether it is smaller than an ant or larger than it. In addition, all of that is in a clear record, i.e., in the Preserved Tablet. For this knowledge, power and mercy, He alone deserves to be worshipped and taken as God, to the exclusion of all His creation.

Guidance of the verses:

1- The affirmation of revelation and its establishment for the Prophet (ﷺ).

2- Prohibition and permission belong to the right of Allah the Exalted alone, to the exclusion of all His creatures.

3- The prohibition of lying against Allah, and that its perpetrator deserves punishment.

4- How great are Allah's blessings upon His servants, yet despite this, few of them give thanks.

5- The obligation of being mindful of Allah the Exalted, and the prohibition of heedlessness in that.

6- The affirmation of the Preserved Tablet, as stated in the verses and hadiths.

*Inna awliyā' Allāh* (إن أولياء الله): plural of *walī*, meaning the God-fearing believer, on condition that his faith and piety rest upon a light from God.

*Lā khawfun 'alayhim* (لا خوف عليهم): i.e., they do not fear at death or after it, nor do they grieve over what they left behind after their death.

*Āmanū* (آمنوا): i.e., they affirmed belief in God, in what came from God, in the Messenger of God, and in what the Messenger of God ﷺ informed of.

*Yattaqūn* (يتقون): i.e., they guard against what angers God the Exalted, such as abandoning an obligation or committing a prohibited act.

*Lahumu l-bushrā* (لهم البشرى): i.e., the good news of Paradise in the Qur'an, at death, and through a righteous dream that the person sees or that is seen for him.

*Lā tabdīla li-kalimāt Allāh* (لا تبديل لكلمات الله): i.e., His promise to His righteous servants, for a promise is a word, and the word of God cannot be changed.

*Al-fawz* (الفوز): deliverance from the Fire and entry into Paradise.

**Meaning of the verses:**

God informs, emphasizing the report with the interjection ﴿ألاۤ﴾ and the emphatic particle ﴿إنَّ﴾, saying: ﴿Indeed, the allies of God—no fear will be upon them, nor will they grieve﴾. That is, they do not fear at death, nor in the barzakh, nor on the Day of Resurrection, and they do not grieve over what they leave behind after their death, nor in the Hereafter. God then identifies His allies and describes them, saying: ﴿those who believed and used to be God-conscious﴾. That is, they believed in Him, in His Messenger, and in everything His Messenger brought from his Lord, and they were mindful throughout their lives and all their moments of what angers God the Exalted, so they do not abandon an obligation they are able to perform, nor do they approach a prohibition they were not compelled to commit. As for His words, ﴿For them is good news﴾ in the life of this world and in the Hereafter: that is, for them is the good news from their Lord in His Book of His pleasure and entry into Paradise. They also have this good news at the time of death, when the angels give them tidings of God's pleasure and His Garden, and in the Hereafter, when they rise from their graves, the angels meet them with glad tidings.

His words, ﴿There is no alteration to the words of God﴾, are a confirmation of what He gave them as good news, since that good news was by the words of God, and the words of God are not changed; so God's promise does not fail.

1. The guardianship of God is attained through obedience to Him and conformity to what He loves and dislikes. Whoever believes in a manner pleasing to God and fears God in performing the obligations and avoiding the prohibitions has become a friend of God, and God is his Friend.

2. The good news is what God honors one with through a righteous dream that the guardian sees or that is seen for him.

3. The allies of God are the people of faith and piety; the disbeliever and the wicked person can never be an ally, unless the disbeliever believes and the wicked person becomes righteous by doing good deeds and abstaining from what is forbidden.

4. The truthfulness of God's reports and the justice of His rulings, and the secret of His guardianship: it revolves around conformity to the Lord, the Exalted, in what is obligatory of beliefs, actions, words, essences and attributes, and in what is disliked of these. Whoever agrees with his Lord has befriended Him, and whoever opposes Him has become His enemy.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 10, verses 65–67:

Explanation of the words:

*La yahzunka*: That is, let not their speech make you grieve.

*Inna al-'izzata lillah*: Al-'izzah (might) means dominance and subjugation.

*Shuraka'*: That is, partners in truth who possess, alongside Allah, benefit or harm for those who worship them.

*Illa al-zann*: Al-zann (conjecture) is weaker than doubt (shakk).

*Yakhrusun*: That is, they guess and lie.

*Li-taskunu fihi*: That is, you rest in it, finding repose and stillness from movement.

*Mubsiran*: That is, luminous, in which all things are seen.

*Fi dhalika*: That is, in His, exalted be He, making the night a time of rest and the day illuminated, are signs (*li-ayat*).

*Yasma'un*: That is, hearing of responsiveness and acceptance.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues to establish the three matters of tawhid: tawhid (divine oneness), prophethood, and resurrection. The Exalted says, addressing His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿And let not their speech grieve you﴾, that is, let not the words of the polytheists who fabricate, ﴿You are not a messenger﴾ [al-Ra'd: 43], and that you are ﴿a poet, possessed﴾ [al-Saffat: 36], cause you grief. For this speech of theirs yields them nothing but evil consequence and inevitable defeat. ﴿Indeed, all might belongs to Allah﴾: your Lord, the Strong, the Capable, will defeat them and grant you victory over them. So be patient with what they say, do not despair, and do not grieve. Indeed, He, exalted be He, is the All-Hearing of the speech of His servants, the All-Knowing of their deeds and conditions, and nothing of their affairs is hidden from Him. ﴿Unquestionably, to Allah belongs whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth﴾ in creation, dominion, and disposal. Everything is in His grip and under His authority and subjugation, so how would you, O our Messenger, be concerned about them, grieving over their words? ﴿And those who call upon other than Allah do not follow partners﴾, that is, gods in truth, such that they deserve worship by virtue of possessing benefit or harm, death or life. Rather, in their worship they follow nothing but conjecture ﴿and they are not but guessing﴾, that is, they fabricate and lie. As for His saying, ﴿It is He who made for you the night that you may rest therein and the day as something visible﴾, that is, the true God who must be called upon and worshipped is Allah, who made for you, O people, a dark night so that you may rest in it and be relieved of the toil of work by day, and made for you the day illuminated, that is, luminous, so that you can work in it and secure for yourselves what you need in life of food and clothing. Those idols and images are not worthy of divinity such that they should be called upon and worshipped. His saying, ﴿Indeed, in that are signs for a people who hear﴾, that is, in what the Exalted has mentioned of His perfection, His might, His power, and His management of the affairs of His creation are clear signs and indications that there is no god but Him and no lord other than Him. But those signs are perceived only by one who hears with acceptance and response, not by one who hears the sound without reflecting on it or pondering its meanings, for such a person is like a blind man who does not see and a deaf man who does not hear.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- The believer who calls to Allah, the Exalted, must not let the speech and falsehoods of the people of falsehood grieve him, lest he cease his call, and let him know that all might belongs to Allah and that He will honour him with it and humble his enemies.

2- What is worshipped besides Allah has no proof established by its worshippers, nor do they possess any argument for it; rather, they are imitators following conjectures and delusions.

3- The manifestations of Allah's power in creation and management are sufficient to establish that worship belongs to Him alone and to negate it from anything else.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 10, verses 68–70:

Explanation of the words:

Subhanahu (Glorified is He): that is, He is exalted above any imperfection and above having a son.

Al-Ghaniyy (the Self-Sufficient): that is, absolute self-sufficiency, such that He has no need of anything.

In talan min sultan ('You have no authority for this'): that is, you have no proof or evidence for it.

Bihadha (for this): that is, what you say, namely the attribution of a son to Allah, exalted is He.

Mata' fi al-dunya (a brief enjoyment in this world): that is, what they are in today is nothing but a brief enjoyment; they will die and lose everything.

Yakfuruna (they disbelieve): that is, by attributing a son to Allah, exalted is He, and by worshipping other than Allah, glorified is He.

Meaning of the verses:

The context still concerns the affirmation and establishment of Tawhid (affirmation of the Oneness of Allah) by refuting shirk (associating partners with Allah) and its doubts. Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿They say: "Allah has taken a son." Glorified is He﴾. That is, the polytheists said that the angels are the daughters of Allah, a saying that grieves the Messenger ﷺ, like their saying to him ﴿You are not a messenger﴾ [al-Ra'd: 43]. The Prophet ﷺ was forbidden to grieve over the corrupt and false sayings of the polytheists. Allah exalted Himself above this lie, saying "Glorified is He," and established the proof against the polytheists' claim by declaring that He is the Self-Sufficient (al-Ghaniyy), with an essential self-sufficiency, such that one needs nothing else alongside Him. How then would He need a son or daughter so as to be supported by him, when He is the Self-Sufficient, the Praiseworthy? Another proof of His self-sufficiency is that to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth; all are His creation and His possession. Is it conceivable that a master and owner would take one of his slaves as a son? Another argument: do those who claim that Allah has a son have any proof establishing that? The answer is no, no. Allah, exalted is He, says, rebuking them: ﴿You have no authority for this﴾, that is, you have no proof or evidence for what you say. Then He reproved and rebuked them by saying: ﴿Do you say about Allah what you do not know?﴾ And He commanded His Messenger ﷺ to declare, announcing the failure and loss of the liars: ﴿Indeed, those who invent falsehood against Allah will not succeed.﴾ If it is said: how will they not succeed when they enjoy wealth, children, status and authority at times? The answer lies in His saying ﴿A brief enjoyment in this world﴾, that is, they have a brief enjoyment in this world, which they enjoy until the end of their lives; then to Allah is their return, all of them; then He will make them taste the severe punishment, through which they will forget everything they enjoyed in the worldly life. Allah explained the severe punishment He makes them taste by their disbelief, saying: ﴿because they used to disbelieve﴾, that is, they denied Allah's perfection and self-sufficiency, so they attributed to Him a son and a partner.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The disbelief of one who attributes to Allah any imperfection, such as a son or a partner, or incapacity in any form.

2- Every claim for which its holder does not establish a decisive proof and clear evidence has no value and is not to be regarded.

3- Those who lie against Allah, such as charlatans, sorcerers, and people of innovations and superstitions, will not succeed, and their end is loss.

4- The believer should not be deceived by the enjoyments, abundance of provision, and bodily health that people of falsehood and evil display, for that is the enjoyment of the worldly life; then their affair will end in lasting loss.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 10, verses 68–70:

Explanation of the words:

Subhanahu (Glorified is He): that is, He is exalted above any imperfection and above having a son.

Al-Ghaniyy (the Self-Sufficient): that is, absolute self-sufficiency, such that He has no need of anything.

In talan min sultan ('You have no authority for this'): that is, you have no proof or evidence for it.

Bihadha (for this): that is, what you say, namely the attribution of a son to Allah, exalted is He.

Mata' fi al-dunya (a brief enjoyment in this world): that is, what they are in today is nothing but a brief enjoyment; they will die and lose everything.

Yakfuruna (they disbelieve): that is, by attributing a son to Allah, exalted is He, and by worshipping other than Allah, glorified is He.

Meaning of the verses:

The context still concerns the affirmation and establishment of Tawhid (affirmation of the Oneness of Allah) by refuting shirk (associating partners with Allah) and its doubts. Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿They say: "Allah has taken a son." Glorified is He﴾. That is, the polytheists said that the angels are the daughters of Allah, a saying that grieves the Messenger ﷺ, like their saying to him ﴿You are not a messenger﴾ [al-Ra'd: 43]. The Prophet ﷺ was forbidden to grieve over the corrupt and false sayings of the polytheists. Allah exalted Himself above this lie, saying "Glorified is He," and established the proof against the polytheists' claim by declaring that He is the Self-Sufficient (al-Ghaniyy), with an essential self-sufficiency, such that one needs nothing else alongside Him. How then would He need a son or daughter so as to be supported by him, when He is the Self-Sufficient, the Praiseworthy? Another proof of His self-sufficiency is that to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth; all are His creation and His possession. Is it conceivable that a master and owner would take one of his slaves as a son? Another argument: do those who claim that Allah has a son have any proof establishing that? The answer is no, no. Allah, exalted is He, says, rebuking them: ﴿You have no authority for this﴾, that is, you have no proof or evidence for what you say. Then He reproved and rebuked them by saying: ﴿Do you say about Allah what you do not know?﴾ And He commanded His Messenger ﷺ to declare, announcing the failure and loss of the liars: ﴿Indeed, those who invent falsehood against Allah will not succeed.﴾ If it is said: how will they not succeed when they enjoy wealth, children, status and authority at times? The answer lies in His saying ﴿A brief enjoyment in this world﴾, that is, they have a brief enjoyment in this world, which they enjoy until the end of their lives; then to Allah is their return, all of them; then He will make them taste the severe punishment, through which they will forget everything they enjoyed in the worldly life. Allah explained the severe punishment He makes them taste by their disbelief, saying: ﴿because they used to disbelieve﴾, that is, they denied Allah's perfection and self-sufficiency, so they attributed to Him a son and a partner.

4- The believer should not be deceived by the enjoyments, abundance of provision, and bodily health that people of falsehood and evil display, for that is the enjoyment of the worldly life; then their affair will end in lasting loss.

**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 10, verses 71–73:**

**Explanation of the words:**

*"Wa-tlu 'alayhim naba' Nuh"* (And recite to them the news of Noah): i.e., recite to the polytheists the news of Noah, that is, his great and momentous account.

*"Kabura 'alaykum maqami"* (My standing [among you] has been grievous to you): i.e., my standing among you, calling to my Lord, has been great upon you.

*"Fa-ajmi'u amrakum"* (So resolve upon your affair): i.e., determine a firm resolve.

*"Ghummah"* (distress): i.e., concealment and confusion, such that you do not find guidance from it to what you desire.

*"Thumma iqḍu ilayya"* (Then carry out [your decision] against me): i.e., execute your command.

*"Wa-la tundhirun"* (And do not give me respite): i.e., do not delay me out of mercy towards me or compassion for me.

*"Fa-in tawallaytum"* (But if you turn away): i.e., you turn away from what I call you to of monotheism.

*"Fi al-fulk"* (In the ark): i.e., in the ship.

*"Khala'if"* (successors): i.e., each one succeeds the previous one, generation after generation.

**The meaning of the verses:**

The noble context continues in seeking the guidance of the polytheists, by answering their claims and explaining the truth to them. In these verses, Allah the Exalted commands His Messenger ﷺ to recite to them a portion of the story of Noah with his polytheist people, whose condition was exactly like that of the polytheists of the Arabs. In reciting this account there are two benefits: the first is consolation for the Messenger and encouraging him to be patient; the second is alerting the polytheists to their error and warning them against persisting in polytheism and disobedience, lest there befall them the punishment that befell others. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And recite to them the news of Noah﴾, i.e., his account of great significance, which is his saying to them: ﴿O my people, if my standing [among you] and my reminding you of the signs of Allah has been grievous to you, then upon Allah I have relied﴾, i.e., my presence among you, calling you to Allah and reminding you of the signs of Allah, has been great and burdensome upon you. Indeed I have put my trust in Allah. ﴿So resolve upon your affair﴾, i.e., determine a firm resolve, and call upon your partners too for help. ﴿Then let not your affair be concealed from you⁠—﴾, i.e., let it not be obscure and confused for you, causing you to hesitate in carrying out what you have resolved. ﴿Then carry out [your decision] against me and do not give me respite﴾, i.e., do not delay me at all, whether by killing me or banishing me. His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿But if you turn away﴾, i.e., you turn away from my call and admonition and do not accept what I call you to, which is the worship of Allah alone, ﴿then I have not asked you for any reward﴾, i.e., any recompense, so that you would turn away on that account. ﴿My reward is only from my Lord, who sent me and charged me, and He has commanded me to be among the Muslims﴾, whose hearts, faces and all their deeds are for Him. So I too, all my work is for Him, and I do not seek any wage from anyone else. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿But they denied him﴾, i.e., he called them and persisted in calling them to Allah for a long time, and the end was that they denied him. So We saved him and those with him among the believers in the ark, and We made them successors, one succeeding the other. And We drowned those who denied Our signs which We sent with Our servant Noah. So look, O Our Messenger, at how was the end of those who were warned, who did not accept advice and did not respond to the truth. Indeed, it was a grievous end: drowning in the flood, fire in Hell, and loss. Allah the Exalted said in Surah Nuh: ﴿Because of their sins they were drowned and then made to enter a Fire, and they found for themselves, besides Allah, no helpers﴾ [Verse 25].

**Guidance from the verses:**

From the guidance of the verses:

1- Consolation for the callers to Allah through the example of Noah's great stance when he said to his people: "Resolve upon your affair and carry out what you intend; indeed I have relied upon Allah."

2- The fruit of trust in Allah is courage, tranquility of soul, patience and endurance, together with firmness of resolve.

3- A caller to Allah should not take a wage for his call except in cases of necessity.

4- Clarification of the evil end of those who deny, after they have been warned and admonished.

**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 10, verses 74–78:**

**Explanation of the words:**

*Bil-bayyinat* (with clear proofs): that is, with clear proofs of the truth of their call and of what they called to, namely the Oneness of God, may He be exalted.

*Natba'* (We seal): sealing upon the heart is the accumulation of sins upon the heart until faith finds no way to reach it.

*Al-mu'tadin* (the transgressors): those who exceed the limit in wrongdoing and in trespassing against the bounds of the Sharia.

*Al-haqq* (the truth): the signs brought by Musa, peace be upon him, and they are nine.

*Litalfitana* (to turn us away): to turn us aside and divert our faces from what we found our fathers upon.

*Al-kibriya'* (greatness): that is, exaltation, lordship, and dominion over people.

**The meaning of the verses:**

When the Exalted mentioned a portion of the story of Nuh, peace be upon him, in which He highlighted the manifestation of reliance upon God from Nuh, to be followed, and the manifestation of God's support for His allies and defeat of His enemies, He here mentioned one of His customs with His creation: that He sent after Nuh many messengers to their peoples, and they came to them with clear proofs, that is, with arguments and demonstrations of their truthfulness and the soundness of what they brought and called to of the Oneness of God. Yet those peoples would not have believed in what those before them had denied, from Nuh. The Exalted said: ﴿Thus do We seal upon the hearts of the transgressors﴾. This is an explanation of God's custom regarding mankind: that when a servant sins and persists in sin without repentance, the sin becomes a disposition of his, which he cannot part with. Sin is nothing but transgression against the bounds of the Lawgiver. Whoever transgresses, and transgresses again, and persists in transgression, acquires that disposition, and the seal is placed upon the heart, so that it no longer accepts faith, nor recognizes good, nor denounces evil.

And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Then after them We sent Musa and Harun﴾, that is, after the destroyed nations, We sent Our two messengers, Musa and Harun, the sons of Imran, to Pharaoh and his chiefs with Our signs containing the evidence of the soundness of the demand of Our two messengers, which is the Oneness of God, and the sending of the Children of Israel with them. ﴿But they were arrogant﴾, that is, Pharaoh and his chiefs. ﴿And they were a people of criminals﴾, in that they corrupted hearts and minds, shed blood, and tortured the weak. The Exalted says of them: ﴿So when the truth came to them from Us, they said: "Indeed, this is manifest magic."﴾ That is, when the miracles overwhelmed them, and the signs of Musa were the miracles that overthrew their falsehood, they said, "Indeed this is manifest magic," as a way of escaping the defeat that had befallen them. Musa answered them with His saying: ﴿Do you say of the truth when it has come to you: "This is magic"?﴾ Then, after rebuking them, he proved the falsity of their claim by his having prevailed over them and triumphed against them, so he said: ﴿Is this magic? And the magicians do not succeed.﴾ That is, if what I brought were magic, how did I succeed in nullifying your magic and defeating your magicians? When he silenced them with proof, they said evasively: ﴿Have you come to us to turn us away﴾, that is, to divert us ﴿from that upon which we found our fathers, and that you two may have greatness in the land﴾, that is, that you two may have sovereignty and dominion in the land of Egypt. Thus they followed the path of political accusation. And they said: ﴿And we will not believe you two﴾, that is, we will not confirm you nor follow you.

**Guidance from the verses:**

1. Explanation of God's custom regarding mankind: that plunging deeply into evil, corruption and wrongdoing necessitates the sealing of hearts, so the servant is deprived of faith and guidance.

2. Condemnation of arrogance, and that it is a cause of much criminality.

3. Affirmation that the one who practices magic never succeeds, nor attains his goal, nor escapes what he fears.

4. False accusations are the way of the people of falsehood, wrongdoing and corruption.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 10, verses 79–82:

Explanation of the words:

"Sahir 'alim" (a skilled sorcerer): i.e., one who possesses true sorcery, with a real effect, and is knowledgeable in the craft.

"Alqu" (throw): i.e., cast into the arena whatever you wish to cast of the various kinds of sorcery.

"Inna Allah sayubtiluhu" (Indeed, Allah will nullify it): i.e., He will make its falsehood manifest before the onlookers among the people.

"Wa yuhiqqu Allah al-haqq" (And Allah will establish the truth): i.e., He will confirm and make firm the truth.

"Bi-kalimatihi" (by His words): i.e., by His command, for He says to a thing, "Be," and it is.

"Al-mujrimun" (the criminals): those who commit crime against themselves and against others, namely the wrongdoers and corrupters.

Meaning of the verses:

The narrative remains on the story of Musa after the story of Nuh, peace be upon them both, in the preceding verses. When Musa overcame Pharaoh and his chiefs with proof, Pharaoh accused Musa and his brother Harun of being political figures who wanted kingship and dominion over the land, with no concern but that. Pharaoh lied, for he was among the liars. Here, he ordered the men of his state to bring him the scholars of sorcery, so that they might rival Musa in sorcery. He gathered his sorcerers, and Musa said to them, "Throw what you are going to throw." So they threw their ropes and their staffs, and said, "By the might of Pharaoh, we are indeed the victors." Musa looked at them and said: "What you have brought is sorcery. Indeed, Allah will nullify it. Indeed, Allah does not set right the work of the corrupters. And Allah will establish the truth by His words, even if the criminals dislike it." Then he cast his staff, and behold, it swallowed up what they had falsely fabricated, so the truth was established and what they had been doing was nullified.

Lessons from the verses:

1- Sorcery has ways by which it is learned, and it has scholars who know it. Learning it is forbidden, and practicing it is forbidden.

2- The penalty for a sorcerer is death, because it is corruption on the earth.

3- It is permissible to challenge the enemy and to contend with him to manifest the truth and nullify falsehood.

4- The outcome of corruption, and the deeds of its people, is ruin and destruction.

5- Whenever truth confronts falsehood, falsehood is defeated and truth triumphs, by the command of Allah the Exalted and His true promise.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 10, verses 83–87:

Explanation of the words:

Fa-ma amana li-Musa: that is, they did not submit to him and follow him.

Illa dhurriyyatun: that is, a small group of the children of the Children of Israel.

Wa-mala'ihim: that is, their nobles and leaders.

An yaftinahum: that he would persecute and torment them.

La-'alin fi al-ardh: dominating, tyrannical.

Muslimin: submitting and yielding to His command and prohibition.

Fitnatan lil-qawm al-zalimin: that is, do not expose them to trial by Your giving us victory over them, so that they see that they are better than us and increase in disbelief.

An tabawwa'a: take for your people in Egypt houses to which you return and in which you dwell.

Qiblah: that is, places of worship in which you pray.

Meaning of the verses:

After the dazzling victory that Musa achieved over the magicians, and the bitter defeat that befell Pharaoh, none believed in Musa and followed him except a small group of the Children of Israel and a few of the family of Pharaoh, such as his wife, the believer of Pharaoh's family, and the hairdresser. Almighty God said: ﴿So none believed in Musa except a small group from his people, out of fear of Pharaoh﴾, that is, together with fear of Pharaoh that he would persecute them. His saying ﴿and their nobles﴾ refers to the believers among Pharaoh's family, that is, along with fear of their nobles and leaders that they too would persecute them. God Almighty's saying ﴿Indeed, Pharaoh was a tyrant in the land﴾ means he was dominant, domineering, and a tyrannical oppressor, ﴿and indeed he was among the transgressors﴾ in wrongdoing, which is why they feared him when they believed. When fear appeared among the Children of Israel, Musa said to them ﴿O my people, if you have believed in God, then rely upon Him, if you are Muslims﴾. So entrust your affair to Him, if you are truly submitting to God, yielding to His command and prohibition. They answered, saying ﴿In God we have put our trust﴾, and asked God Almighty not to expose the people of Pharaoh to trial by them, by giving them victory over them so that they would increase in disbelief and wrongdoing. This includes that He not empower the wrongdoers over us, so that they would tempt us in our religion by turning us away from it through the force of torture: ﴿Our Lord, do not make us a trial for the wrongdoing people, and save us by Your mercy from the disbelieving people﴾. This is a fine means of seeking nearness they employed, for they said "by Your mercy," so they sought nearness to God through His mercy, that He might answer their supplication. The intended "disbelieving people" here are Pharaoh and his chiefs. God Almighty's saying ﴿And We revealed to Musa and his brother﴾, that is, Harun, ﴿that you should settle your people in Egypt in houses, and make your houses a qiblah﴾, that is, facing one another, and places of worship in which you pray, ﴿and establish the prayer﴾ in the manner prescribed for you.

This is based on the fact that after the victory over Pharaoh, the Children of Israel began to withdraw from Pharaoh's society, so they were commanded to become a self-governing community in preparation for leaving the land of Egypt. The Lord, blessed and exalted, commanded them to make their houses a qiblah, that is, facing one another, so that they would know who enters upon them and who leaves from among them, and so that they could pray in them as in mosques, since they had been prevented from the mosques, either by their destruction or by being barred from them through injustice and aggression. God Almighty's saying ﴿And give good tidings to the believers﴾, that is, give good tidings, O our Messenger, to the sincere believers who are perfect in their faith, of a good end, with honour in this world and happiness in the Hereafter, by entering the Abode of Peace.

Guidance from the verses:

1. Consolation for the Messenger ﷺ, in showing him how Musa triumphed through miracles, and yet only a few of his people followed him.

2. Condemnation of haughtiness on earth and of excess in evil and corruption, and of those who engage in them.

3. The obligation of trusting in God to bear the burden of calling to God and to carry out obedience to Him.

4. The legitimacy of supplication and seeking nearness to God through His names and attributes.

5. Taking places of worship in homes for prayer when fearful.

6. The obligation of establishing the prayer.

7. God's good tidings to believers and to those who establish the prayer of a good end in both abodes.

1. Consolation for the Messenger ﷺ, in showing him how Musa triumphed through miracles, and yet only a few of his people followed him.

3. The obligation of trusting in God to bear the burden of calling to God and to carry out obedience to Him.

4. The legitimacy of supplication and seeking nearness to God through His names and attributes.

5. Taking places of worship in homes for prayer when fearful.

6. The obligation of establishing the prayer.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 10, verses 88–89:

Explanation of the words:

Zinah (adornment): jewelry, fine garments, household furnishings and goods.

Amwalan (wealth): that is, abundant gold, silver, livestock and crops.

Ut-mis (obliterate): remove its trace from among them by destroying it.

Washdud 'ala qulubihim (harden their hearts): bind upon them so that faith never enters them, so that they perish while disbelieving.

Ujibat da'watukuma (your supplication has been answered): that is, Allah the Exalted has accepted it.

Fastaqima (so go straight): stand firm in obedience to Allah by carrying out His message, calling to Him, and being patient with the harm done for His sake.

Sabil alladhina la ya'lamun (the way of those who do not know): that is, the path of the ignorant, who do not recognize what Allah loves and what displeases Him, and who do not know the laws of Allah which He sent down to His servants.

Meaning of the two verses:

The context continues with the story of Musa (Moses) with Fir'awn (Pharaoh) and the Children of Israel. After Fir'awn persisted in obstinacy and arrogance following his defeat, Musa asked his Lord, saying: ﴿Our Lord, You have indeed given Pharaoh and his chiefs﴾, that is, You have bestowed upon them ﴿adornment﴾, meaning what they adorn themselves with: clothing, furnishings, household goods, and various kinds of jewelry and fine garments; and His saying ﴿and wealth﴾, that is, gold, silver, livestock and crops ﴿in the life of this world﴾, that is, in this worldly life. And His saying: ﴿Our Lord, that they may lead astray from Your way﴾, that is, so that by this they would be led into error. ﴿Our Lord, obliterate their wealth﴾, that is, destroy its trace by wiping it out and making it unfit for benefit, ﴿and harden their hearts﴾, that is, seal their hearts and make them firm, so that they do not believe until they see the painful torment that hurts most severely. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Your supplication has indeed been answered, so go straight﴾ in obedience to Us, by calling to Us, performing Our worship, giving sincere counsel to Our servants, and working to rescue Our servants from the oppression of the oppressors. ﴿And do not follow the way of those who do not know﴾, that is, do not hasten the coming of the punishment, for those who do not know the wisdom, plans, decree and divine measure of Allah hasten Allah in regard to His promise to them. So do not be like them; rather, wait for Our promise and be patient until the promise of Allah comes. Allah does not fail in His promise.

Guidance from the two verses:

From the guidance of the two verses:

1- The legitimacy of supplicating for the destruction of the people of injustice.

2- Abundance of wealth and kinds of adornment, and immersing oneself in them and being distracted by them, causes its possessor to go astray.

3- Those who reach a degree of evil and corruption upon whose hearts a seal is set do not die except in disbelief, and so they lose.

4- The one who says "Amin" is a supplicant, and so he is a partner in the supplication. Therefore the people of the mosque say "Amin" to the Imam's supplication in the khutbah, so the answer is obtained for all. From here, those who circumambulate or visit (the shrines) err, for they supplicate with the supplication of the guide and do not say "Amin."

5- The prohibition of following the paths of the people of misguidance, and imitating the ignorant and going after them.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 10, verses 90–92:

Explanation of the words:

*Wa jawaznā bi-Banī Isrā'īl* (And We brought the Children of Israel across): i.e., We caused them to cross the sea until they had passed over it.

*Al-baḥr* (the sea): the Sea of Qulzum (the Red Sea).

*Baghyan wa 'adwan* (in rebellion and transgression): i.e., out of rebellion against Mūsā and Hārūn and aggression against them both.

*Ālān* (Now?): i.e., at this time do you affirm the Oneness of God and acknowledge your own humiliation?!

*Bi-badanika* (in your body): i.e., in your physical body, with no spirit in it.

*Āya* (a sign): a proof that you are a servant and not a lord, so that people may take warning from it.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues with the story of Mūsā and Hārūn with Pharaoh and the Children of Israel. God, the Exalted, says: ﴿And We brought the Children of Israel across the sea﴾. This is the beginning of God's answering the supplication of Mūsā and Hārūn. The meaning of ﴿jāwaznā﴾ is: We caused them to cross the sea until they had passed over it. This came about when Mūsā was commanded to strike the sea with his staff, and he struck it, and the sea split apart, so that each division was like a great mountain, and the ground became dry. Mūsā entered with the Children of Israel, with Jibrīl (peace be upon him) leading them on a horse, until they both crossed the sea to the shore. Pharaoh came on his horse with thousands of soldiers, and they followed Mūsā and the Children of Israel and entered the sea. When they reached its middle, God, the Exalted, closed the sea over them, and they all drowned, except for Pharaoh. When drowning overtook him, that is, when it reached him and the water rose to his neck, he declared his repentance, saying: ﴿I believe that there is no god except the One in whom the Children of Israel believe﴾. Yet, out of his arrogance, he did not say "there is no god but God." Had he said it, God would have accepted his repentance and saved him. Instead he said: ﴿there is no god except the One in whom the Children of Israel believe﴾, while knowing that He is God. His saying ﴿and I am of the Muslims﴾ was an exaggerated plea for deliverance from drowning through repentance, in which he declared that he was among the Muslims, that is, those who submit and yield to His command. God replied with His words: ﴿Now?﴾, that is, at the time of repentance and submission after disbelief, ﴿while you had disobeyed before﴾ and rebelled against God and His law, and disbelieved in Him and His Messenger, ﴿and you were of the corrupters﴾ of the lands and their people through oppression, evil and corruption. ﴿So today We will save you﴾, that is, We will place you upon a high place of the earth, that is, something elevated from it, ﴿in your body﴾, that is, your physical body without your spirit, ﴿so that you may be a sign for those after you﴾, or those who come after you among people, ﴿a sign﴾, that is, a proof that you are a created, subjugated servant, and not, as you claimed, a lord and worshipped god, and so that it may be a lesson to others, so that they do not transgress as you transgressed and do not disbelieve as you disbelieved, lest they perish as you perished. God's words: ﴿And indeed, many of the people are heedless of Our signs﴾ are a report from Him about the reality of people. Among those heedless ones are the people of Makkah, the disbelieving Quraysh, to whom these signs are recited, and this narrative was only related for their guidance, if only they would be guided.

Guidance from the verses:

1. Repentance is not accepted at the moment of witnessing the punishment. In the hadith: "The repentance of a servant is accepted as long as he has not yet reached the death rattle (lam yughargir)."

2. The most perfect and excellent religion is Islam; for this reason, people of certainty ask God, the Exalted, to cause them to die as Muslims. When Pharaoh became certain of his destruction, he claimed to be a Muslim.

3. The virtue of *lā ilāha illā Allāh* (there is no god but God): it is reported that Jibrīl would stand between Pharaoh and saying "There is no god but God," so that he might be saved, but he did not say it and drowned, being among the lost.

4. Confirmation of a reality: that most people in this life are heedless of what is intended for them and for their benefit, and they do not awaken until they perish.

Yet, out of his arrogance, he did not say "there is no god but God." Had he said it, God would have accepted his repentance and saved him. Instead he said: ﴿there is no god except the One in whom the Children of Israel believe﴾, while knowing that He is God. His saying ﴿and I am of the Muslims﴾ was an exaggerated plea for deliverance from drowning through repentance, in which he declared that he was among the Muslims, that is, those who submit and yield to His command. God replied with His words: ﴿Now?﴾, that is, at the time of repentance and submission after disbelief, ﴿while you had disobeyed before﴾ and rebelled against God and His law, and disbelieved in Him and His Messenger, ﴿and you were of the corrupters﴾ of the lands and their people through oppression, evil and corruption. ﴿So today We will save you﴾, that is, We will place you upon a high place of the earth, that is, something elevated from it, ﴿in your body﴾, that is, your physical body without your spirit, ﴿so that you may be a sign for those after you﴾, or those who come after you among people, ﴿a sign﴾, that is, a proof that you are a created, subjugated servant, and not, as you claimed, a lord and worshipped god, and so that it may be a lesson to others, so that they do not transgress as you transgressed and do not disbelieve as you disbelieved, lest they perish as you perished. God's words: ﴿And indeed, many of the people are heedless of Our signs﴾ are a report from Him about the reality of people. Among those heedless ones are the people of Makkah, the disbelieving Quraysh, to whom these signs are recited, and this narrative was only related for their guidance, if only they would be guided.

Guidance from the verses:

1. Repentance is not accepted at the moment of witnessing the punishment. In the hadith: "The repentance of a servant is accepted as long as he has not yet reached the death rattle (lam yughargir)."

2. The most perfect and excellent religion is Islam; for this reason, people of certainty ask God, the Exalted, to cause them to die as Muslims. When Pharaoh became certain of his destruction, he claimed to be a Muslim.

3. The virtue of *lā ilāha illā Allāh* (there is no god but God): it is reported that Jibrīl would stand between Pharaoh and saying "There is no god but God," so that he might be saved, but he did not say it and drowned, being among the lost.

4. Confirmation of a reality: that most people in this life are heedless of what is intended for them and for their benefit, and they do not awaken until they perish.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 10, verse 93:

Explanation of the words:

Mubawwa' sidq (a dwelling of truth): that is, We settled them in a good, pure and pleasing abode.

Min al-tayyibat (of the good things): that is, of the kinds of good, lawful provision.

Hatta ja'ahumu al-'ilm (until knowledge came to them): this is their knowledge that Muhammad (ﷺ) is the awaited Prophet and that he is the one who saves.

Yaqdi baynahum (He will judge between them): He will rule between them.

Fima kanu fihi yakhtalifun (concerning that in which they used to differ): that is, concerning the truth on which they differed, so that He admits the believers to Paradise and the disbelievers to the Fire.

The meaning of the noble verse:

This is the conclusion of the discussion about Musa and the Children of Israel, after Allah saved them from their enemy by destroying him in the sea. Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿And We certainly settled the Children of Israel in a dwelling of truth﴾, that is, We settled them in a good, pure and pleasing abode, and this was the land of Palestine in the blessed land of al-Sham. This happened after their deliverance from the wandering (in the desert) and their entry into Palestine in the company of the Prophet of Allah, Yusha' ibn Nun (peace be upon him). His words ﴿and We provided them with good things﴾: for the land of al-Sham is a land of honey, ghee, grains, fruits, meat and [...]. Mentioning this is to show the blessings of Allah, the Exalted, so that they would give thanks for them. His words: ﴿And they did not differ until knowledge came to them﴾ mean that the Children of Israel, whom Allah honoured with that great honour, were, before the mission of the Prophet (ﷺ), agreed upon one religion, awaiting the awaited Prophet promised in the Torah, who would rescue the Children of Israel from the punishment and oppression that had befallen them at the hands of their enemies, the Romans. When he came to them, and he is the knowledge, which is the Qur'an, revealed to Muhammad (ﷺ), they differed: some of them believed in him, and some of them disbelieved. His words, addressing the Prophet (ﷺ), the Exalted: ﴿Indeed your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that in which they used to differ﴾ concern the matter of faith in you, following you, and following what you brought of guidance and the religion of truth, so that He admits the believers to Paradise and the disbelievers enter the Fire.

Guidance from the noble verse:

From the guidance of the noble verse:

1- Explanation of Allah's honouring of the Children of Israel.

2- Good provision is what is lawful, not what is unlawful.

3- When Allah wills the destruction of a nation, they differ because of knowledge, which in origin is a cause of unity and harmony.

4- The prohibition of disputing in religion, since it leads to division, hostility and war.

5- The Day of Resurrection is the Day of Judgement on which Allah, the Exalted, judges between those who differed by His just decree.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 10, verses 94–97:

Explanation of the words:

Shakk (doubt): whatever is opposed to acceptance, so the doubter is one who does not affirm.

Mimma anzalna ilayka (of what We have sent down to you): i.e., regarding the fact that the Children of Israel did not differ except after knowledge had come to them.

Al-Kitab (the Book): i.e., the Torah and the Gospel.

Fa-la takunanna mina al-mumtarin (so do not be among the doubters): i.e., do not be among those who doubt.

Haqqat alayhim (the word of your Lord has come true against them): i.e., the Fire became due for them by the judgment of God in this regard, recorded in the Preserved Tablet.

Hatta yaraw al-adhab (until they see the punishment): i.e., they persist in their denial until they see the punishment, and then they believe when belief no longer benefits them.

Meaning of the verses:

The Exalted establishes the prophethood of His Messenger: ﴿So if you are in doubt about what We have sent down to you, then ask those who have been reading the Book before you﴾, meaning the rabbis of the Jews and the monks of the Christians, for they know your description and attributes in the Torah and the Gospel, that you are the final Prophet and the deliverer, and that whoever believes in you is saved and whoever disbelieves is destroyed. This is by way of hypothesis, and so that others may be stirred to believe; otherwise he ﷺ had said: (I do not doubt and I do not ask). His saying ﴿Indeed, the truth has come to you from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters﴾: the Exalted swears to His Messenger that the truth has come to him from his Lord, which is the established revelation of the true Word, and forbids him to be among the doubters, i.e., those who doubt the soundness of Islam, and that it is the true religion which God refuses except to make manifest over all religion, even though the polytheists dislike it. His saying ﴿And do not be among those who denied the signs of God, lest you be among the losers﴾: He also forbids him to be among those who denied the revelation of God, His law and His Messenger, which are referred to as signs because they carry it and call to it, and so you would be among the losers on the Day of Resurrection. All of this is by way of "I mean you, but my neighbour should hear," since it is impossible for the Messenger to doubt or deny what was sent down to him of the signs carrying the laws and rulings. His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, those against whom the word of your Lord has come true will not believe, even if every sign should come to them﴾: this is as He, the Mighty and Majestic, has informed. Those whom God has decreed to be punished on the Day of Resurrection, and so has written that in the Book of Decrees with Him, will never believe, however much effort is expended for their belief in clarifying the truth, establishing proofs, and displaying evidences against them. In this is consolation for the Messenger of God ﷺ regarding what grieves and saddens him over the opposition of the Quraysh disbelievers and their failure to respond. His saying ﴿even if every sign should come to them﴾ is an emphasis of the preceding ruling, namely that those whom God has judged to enter the Fire will not believe, and will die only as disbelievers, so that God may fulfil what He promised and carry out what He decreed and judged. His saying: ﴿until they see the painful punishment﴾: i.e., they persist in their disbelief in you and in what you have brought until they witness the painful punishment, and at that time they will believe, as Pharaoh believed when drowning overtook him, but his belief did not benefit him. Likewise these polytheists of your people, against whom the word of your Lord has come true, will not believe until they see the painful punishment, and then their belief will not benefit them.

Guidance from the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- Establishing the prophethood of the Messenger ﷺ.

2- Asking those who know is the way for one who does not know.

3- Denying the signs of God is disbelief, and its companion is among the losers.

4- Doubt and fabrication regarding the foundations of religion and its branches is disbelief.

5- Establishing the doctrine of decree and destiny: the wretched is one who is made wretched in the Book of Decrees, and the fortunate is one who is made fortunate therein.

6- The non-acceptance of the repentance of one who witnesses the punishment in this world, by seeing the Angel of Death, and in the Hereafter, after being raised and witnessing the terrors of the Resurrection.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 10, verses 98–100:

Explanation of the words:

Falawla (فلولا): a particle of urging here, meaning "why not" (hallā), carrying a sense of reproach and negation.

Qaryah amanat (قرية آمنت): i.e., the people of a town who believed.

Yunus (يونس): he is Yunus ibn Matta (Jonah son of Matthew), the Prophet and Messenger of Allah.

Ila hin (إلى حين): i.e., until the time their lifespans came to an end.

Afa'anta takrahu al-nas (أفأنت تكره الناس): i.e., you are not able to do that.

Illa bi-idhni Allah (إلا بإذن الله): i.e., by His will and decree.

Al-rijs (الرجس): i.e., the punishment.

The meaning of the verses:

After Allah, exalted is He, mentioned in the preceding verses that loss is inevitable for whoever denies the signs of Allah, and that those who are destined for punishment because their sins encompass them will not believe, since they have lost the readiness to believe, He mentions here what urges the people of Makkah to believe and not to persist in disbelief and denial. So He says: ﴿Why was there not a town that believed, so that its belief benefited it?﴾ That is: why did the people of a town not believe, so that they would benefit from their belief and be saved from the punishment that is due to those who do not believe? That is, why do they not believe, and what prevents them from believing? This is a reproach to them. And His saying ﴿except the people of Yunus; when they believed, We removed from them the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world﴾ means that We did not destroy them with a punishment of annihilation and total destruction, because when they saw the signs of punishment they hastened to repent before it descended upon them, so Allah, exalted is He, removed the punishment from them and gave them enjoyment of life until the end of their lifespans. So what is the matter with the people of Umm al-Qura that they do not repent, as the people of Nineveh in the land of Mosul repented, and they were the people of Yunus, peace be upon him.

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if your Lord had willed, those on earth would have believed, all of them together﴾ carries two implications. The first: that Allah's presenting faith to the people of Makkah, urging them to it, and reproaching them for abandoning it should not be understood to mean that Allah is incapable of making them believe; rather, if He willed their belief, they would have believed, just as if He willed the belief of all who are on earth, they would have believed. The second: consolation for the Messenger and lightening for him the pain and grief of his people's disbelief, while he calls them earnestly and eagerly night and day. So his Lord informed him that if He willed the belief of everyone on earth, they would all have believed; but it is the obligation upon which reward is based, so faith is presented to people as an offering without compulsion. Whoever believes is saved, and whoever does not believe is destroyed. This is indicated by His saying to him: ﴿Will you then compel the people until they become believers?﴾ That is: this is not for you, nor were you charged with it. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And it is not for a soul to believe except by the permission of Allah﴾ is an affirmation and confirmation of what the preceding discourse contained: that faith is not accomplished for anyone except by the will and decree of Allah. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And He places defilement upon those who do not reason﴾ means: although He, exalted is He, calls people to faith, explaining to them its good fruits, and warns them against denial, explaining to them its evil effects, whoever believes, He saves and makes happy; and whoever does not believe, He places the defilement, which is the punishment, encompassing him as a recompense for him, because he does not reason. For had he reasoned, he would not have denied his Lord, disbelieved in Him, disobeyed Him, and rebelled against Him, while He is his Creator and the Owner of his affair.

Guidance from the verses:

Among the guidance of the verses:

1- Among the manifestations of Allah's mercy toward His servants is His calling them to believe in Him and urging them to it.

2- Repentance is accepted before the punishment is witnessed, and seeing the signs does not prevent repentance.

3- Allah's universal will, by which things come into being, never fails, whereas His legislative, obligatory will may be disobeyed.

4- There is no faith except by Allah's permission and decree; therefore the caller should not grieve over people's lack of belief when he has called them and they did not believe, because Allah has eternally decreed their punishment and determined it.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 10, verses 101–103:

Explanation of the Words

ماذا في السماوات والأرض (mā dhā fī as-samāwāt wa-l-arḍ): That is, of the wonders of creation and the striking signs.

وما تغني الآيات والنذر (wa-mā tughnī al-āyāt wa-n-nudhur): That is, they avail nothing at all when the people do not believe.

فهل ينتظرون (fa-hal yantaẓirūn): That is, what do they await?

خلوا من قبلهم (khalaw min qablihim): That is, they passed away before them, from the earlier nations.

قل فانتظروا (qul fa-ntaẓirū): That is, the punishment.

ثم ننجي رسلنا والذين آمنوا (thumma nunajjī rusulanā wa-lladhīna āmanū): That is, from the awaited punishment.

كذلك (kadhālik): That is, in this same manner of deliverance We deliver the believers.

Meaning of the Verses

The context continues with the call to the Quraysh to faith, to tawhid, and to obedience to God and His Messenger ﷺ. God commanded His Messenger to say to them: ﴿Say: Look at what is in the heavens and the earth﴾ of all creatures and the wonders of their making, and the manifestations of wisdom, mercy and power, for these call to belief in God as Lord and God, there is no god but Him and no lord besides Him, and they refute the claim of the divinity of idols and stones. Then He said: ﴿But signs and warnings avail not﴾, that is, the Messengers in guiding a people for whom God has decreed from eternity that they will not believe, even up to what has been determined for them and the punishment in this world and the Hereafter that He has judged against them. But since the knowledge of that belongs to God, the warners must call and exert their utmost effort, and the command belongs to God before and after. And His saying: ﴿Then do they await anything but the like of the days of those who passed away before them?﴾ means: they await only the like of the days of those who passed away before them, from the people of Noah, ʿAd, Thamud and others, whose messengers called them and conveyed to them the message of their Lord, calling them to faith, tawhid and obedience, but they turned away, so God seized them; indeed He is Strong, severe in punishment.

Then God commanded His Messenger to say to them: ﴿So wait﴾, that is, for what has been prescribed for you of punishment if you do not repent to Him and submit, ﴿indeed I am with you among those who wait﴾. If the punishment comes, then the way of God in it is to destroy the wrongdoers, the polytheists, and the deniers, and to deliver His Messengers and the believers. This is the meaning of His saying in the last verse [10:103]: ﴿Then We deliver Our messengers and those who believe. Thus﴾, yes, the deliverance, ﴿it is incumbent upon Us: We deliver the believers.﴾

Lessons from the Verses

From the guidance of these verses:

1- Admonition benefits not a servant who has been decreed from eternity to be among the people of the Fire, however much it is pressed upon him.

2- The wrongdoers in every time and place await nothing but what befell those who wronged before them of disgrace and punishment.

3- God's promise is firmly established for His friends, that He will deliver them from destruction when He destroys the wrongdoing polytheists.
