Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 10, verses 104–107:

Explanation of the words:

Min dini (من ديني): i.e., Islam, in that it is the truth.

Yatawaffakum (يتوفاكم): i.e., He seizes your souls, so He causes you to die.

Wa in aqim wajhaka lil-dini hanifan (وإن أقم وجهك للدين حنيفاً): i.e., my Lord has commanded me to set my face toward the Islamic religion as a hanif (حنيفاً, one who inclines away from all other religions toward it alone and not to anything else).

Ma la yanfa'uka wa la yadurruk (ما لا ينفعك ولا يضرك): i.e., deities that neither benefit nor harm, namely the idols and images of the polytheists.

Innaka idhan min al-zalimin (إنك إذاً من الظالمين): i.e., if you were to call upon them, you would be among the polytheists who wrong themselves.

Fala kashifa lahu illa Hu (فلا كاشف له إلا هو): i.e., there is no remover of harm and no one who repels it from whoever it befalls, except Him, mighty and majestic.

Yusibu bihi (يصيب به): i.e., with bounty and mercy.

Wa Huwa al-Ghafur al-Rahim (وهو الغفور الرحيم): i.e., He forgives the sins of His repentant servants and is merciful to His believing servants.

The meaning of the verses:

After Allah, exalted is He, had explained the path of guidance and the path of misguidance, and had warned, cautioned, promised and threatened in the preceding verses with nothing more to be added, He commanded His Messenger here to confront the polytheists of Makkah and others with the following declaration. He said: ﴿Say, O mankind﴾, i.e., the polytheists of Makkah and the Arabs around them, ﴿if you are in doubt﴾ and uncertainty about the validity of my religion, Islam, which I follow and to which I call, ﴿then I do not worship those you worship besides Allah﴾. So your mere doubt about the validity of my religion does not make me worship idols and images that neither benefit nor harm, ﴿but I worship Allah﴾, who benefits and harms, gives life and causes death, Allah who ﴿causes you to die﴾, i.e., makes you die by seizing your souls. He is the One who must be worshipped, feared and revered. ﴿And I have been commanded to be among the believers﴾, i.e., my Lord commanded me to believe in Him and to be among the believers, so I believed and I am among the believers. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And [I have been commanded] to set your face toward the religion as a hanif, and do not be among the polytheists﴾, i.e., my Lord revealed to me, commanding me to set my face toward His true religion and not to turn toward any other false religion, and He forbade me, emphatically, from being among the polytheists who worship other deities along with Him, after this great proclamation, complete separation, and clear reproach of the people of Makkah for their misguidance and gross error. Allah addressed His Messenger directly, and this is in the manner of "It is you I mean, but hear, O neighbor," so He forbade him, by explicit statement, from calling upon what is other than Allah and neither benefits nor harms him, which is every object of worship other than Allah, mighty and majestic. He said: ﴿And do not call upon, besides Allah, that which neither benefits you nor harms you﴾, i.e., it does not bring you benefit, nor does it ward off harm from you, nor does it harm you by withholding good from you or by sending evil upon you. If you were to do so, by calling upon other than Allah, then ﴿you would indeed be among the wrongdoers﴾. Since calling upon other than Allah is impossible for the Prophet, the statement is an indirect rebuke of the polytheists and a warning to the believers. And His saying, in addressing His Messenger: ﴿And if Allah should touch you with harm, there is no remover of it except Him﴾ from you, mighty and majestic, ﴿and if He should intend for you good, there is no repeller of His bounty﴾, i.e., good such as health, well-being, prosperity and victory. There is no one who can turn it away from you in any circumstance. And His saying: ﴿He causes it to reach whom He wills of His servants﴾, i.e., with bounty, good and blessing, for He is the free chooser who does what He wills and decrees what He desires. And His saying: ﴿And He is the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾ is a statement of His attributes of majesty and perfection, for He forgives the sins of those who repent to Him, however great they may be, and has mercy on His believing servants, however numerous they may be. By this He deserves to be worshipped with love, veneration, obedience and submission.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The believer must not abandon the truth no matter how much people doubt it or cast doubt upon it.

2- The prohibition of polytheism, the obligation to abandon it, and to abandon its adherents.

3- Calling upon other than Allah, whatever the one called upon may be, is forbidden shirk and is never permissible, even if it is named tawassul.

4- A servant does not believe until he is certain that whatever good or evil Allah intends for him, no one can repel it or change it in any circumstance. This is the meaning of the hadith: "What has befallen you would not have missed you, and what has missed you would not have befallen you."

So your mere doubt about the validity of my religion does not make me worship idols and images that neither benefit nor harm, ﴿but I worship Allah﴾, who benefits and harms, gives life and causes death, Allah who ﴿causes you to die﴾, i.e., makes you die by seizing your souls. He is the One who must be worshipped, feared and revered. ﴿And I have been commanded to be among the believers﴾, i.e., my Lord commanded me to believe in Him and to be among the believers, so I believed and I am among the believers. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And [I have been commanded] to set your face toward the religion as a hanif, and do not be among the polytheists﴾, i.e., my Lord revealed to me, commanding me to set my face toward His true religion and not to turn toward any other false religion, and He forbade me, emphatically, from being among the polytheists who worship other deities along with Him, after this great proclamation, complete separation, and clear reproach of the people of Makkah for their misguidance and gross error. Allah addressed His Messenger directly, and this is in the manner of "It is you I mean, but hear, O neighbor," so He forbade him, by explicit statement, from calling upon what is other than Allah and neither benefits nor harms him, which is every object of worship other than Allah, mighty and majestic. He said: ﴿And do not call upon, besides Allah, that which neither benefits you nor harms you﴾, i.e., it does not bring you benefit, nor does it ward off harm from you, nor does it harm you by withholding good from you or by sending evil upon you. If you were to do so, by calling upon other than Allah, then ﴿you would indeed be among the wrongdoers﴾. Since calling upon other than Allah is impossible for the Prophet, the statement is an indirect rebuke of the polytheists and a warning to the believers. And His saying, in addressing His Messenger: ﴿And if Allah should touch you with harm, there is no remover of it except Him﴾ from you, mighty and majestic, ﴿and if He should intend for you good, there is no repeller of His bounty﴾, i.e., good such as health, well-being, prosperity and victory. There is no one who can turn it away from you in any circumstance. And His saying: ﴿He causes it to reach whom He wills of His servants﴾, i.e., with bounty, good and blessing, for He is the free chooser who does what He wills and decrees what He desires. And His saying: ﴿And He is the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾ is a statement of His attributes of majesty and perfection, for He forgives the sins of those who repent to Him, however great they may be, and has mercy on His believing servants, however numerous they may be. By this He deserves to be worshipped with love, veneration, obedience and submission.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The believer must not abandon the truth no matter how much people doubt it or cast doubt upon it.

2- The prohibition of polytheism, the obligation to abandon it, and to abandon its adherents.

3- Calling upon other than Allah, whatever the one called upon may be, is forbidden shirk and is never permissible, even if it is named tawassul.

4- A servant does not believe until he is certain that whatever good or evil Allah intends for him, no one can repel it or change it in any circumstance. This is the meaning of the hadith: "What has befallen you would not have missed you, and what has missed you would not have befallen you."

Ma la yanfa'uka wa la yadurruk (ما لا ينفعك ولا يضرك): i.e., deities that neither benefit nor harm, namely the idols and images of the polytheists.

Fala kashifa lahu illa Hu (فلا كاشف له إلا هو): i.e., there is no remover of harm and no one who repels it from whoever it befalls, except Him, mighty and majestic.

Yusibu bihi (يصيب به): i.e., with bounty and mercy.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 10, verses 108–109:

Explanation of the words:

"O mankind": that is, O people of Makkah.

"The truth has come": that is, the Messenger recites the Qur'an and makes clear the true religion.

"Whoever is guided": that is, whoever believes in Allah and His Messenger and worships Allah alone, having no partner.

"And whoever goes astray": that is, who refuses anything but persistence in polytheism, denial and disobedience.

"Then it is only against himself [that he goes astray]": that is, the burden of straying falls upon the soul of the one who strays, just as the reward of guidance belongs to the soul of the one who is guided.

"And I am not over you a guardian": that is, I am not one who compels you to guidance; rather I am only a conveyer [of the message] and a warner.

"And be patient until Allah judges": that is, concerning the polytheists, by His command.

"And He is the best of judges": that is, in mercy and justice, and in carrying out what He decides, by virtue of His great power.

The meaning of the two verses:

This is the final proclamation in this surah. Allah commands His Messenger to call out to the polytheists with His words: ﴿O mankind﴾, a general address that encompasses all of humanity, though what is meant initially is the people of Makkah. ﴿The truth has certainly come to you from your Lord﴾, namely the Qur'an, which the Messenger of Allah recites, and in which is made clear the true religion, without which a human being cannot attain perfection except through faith in it and sincere adherence to the guidance it contains. Then, whoever is guided through faith and following, the reward of his guidance is for his own self, for it is the self that grows, purifies itself, and becomes fit for the happiness of both abodes. And whoever goes astray through persistence in polytheism, disbelief and denial, then his straying, that is, the requital of his straying, returns upon his own self, for it is the self that becomes corrupted and defiled, and becomes fit for the abhorrence and wrath of Allah and His painful punishment. The Messenger who conveys the message bears no responsibility for this, for his Lord did not entrust him with guiding people; rather He commanded him to declare plainly to them that he is not a guardian over them: ﴿And I am not over you a guardian﴾. The words of the Exalted, ﴿And follow what is revealed to you﴾, are a command to the Prophet ﷺ to hold fast to the truth by following what is revealed to him of commands and prohibitions, and not to neglect any part of that. It implies the corollary, which is not following anything that is not revealed to him by his Lord. And His words, ﴿And be patient until Allah judges, and He is the best of judges﴾, are a command to the Prophet ﷺ to be patient in following the revelation, to remain steadfast in the call, and to bear the harm of the polytheists until the point at which Allah judges concerning them. He has judged, and He commanded him to fight them, so he fought them at Badr and continued fighting them until they submitted to Allah in Islam, and to Allah belongs all praise and grace. His words ﴿and He is the best of judges﴾ are a praise of Allah, that He is the best of those who judge and the most just of those who decide, owing to the perfection of His knowledge, His wisdom, His great power, and His vast mercy.

Lessons from the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- Affirmation that the Qur'an and the Messenger are true, and that Islam is true.

2- Affirmation of the principle that a person is made wretched or happy by his own deeds, not by the deeds of another.

3- The obligation to follow the divine revelation contained in the Qur'an and the authentic Sunnah.

4- The virtue of patience and of awaiting relief from Allah, the Exalted.
